chapters.title: Chapter 103 Division of labor and allocation
paragraphs: "Since our lord has no worries, then what need is there for a strategy?" Jia Xu added a hint of showing off in his tone.
Lu Ming disliked this kind of scholarly arrogance. He rubbed his head. "Wenhe, why not speak more bluntly? I don’t understand."

Faced with such a direct and straightforward lord, Jia Xu was somewhat taken aback. He thought about it and realized it made sense. If the other party hadn’t been so direct and frank, he wouldn’t have switched allegiance to Lu Ming. Even under Dong Zhuo, he had seen the man’s recklessness and pettiness; following Dong Zhuo wouldn’t lead to great things.
Perhaps Jia Xu wasn’t confident in other areas, but he was quite adept at judging people’s appearances and understanding their hearts.

"Our lord is currently enjoying the height of imperial favor. The Yuan family has only two options. One is to send insignificant figures to provoke him, seeking weaknesses to convict him. The other is to send envoys to Longxi County to undermine his power!"

This was something Lu Ming hadn’t considered. After a moment’s thought, he stated directly, "The second point is unnecessary. When I return victorious, His Majesty will need meritorious officials to assist in establishing an heir apparent. There’s no need to worry about them being discarded after their usefulness is over. Hmph, if the Yuan family doesn’t interfere, fine; but if they do, I’ll cut off their hands! Wenhe, in terms of scheming and intrigue, I’m no match for the Yuan family, but often, not everything has to be done according to the rules."
The current emperor has not yet designated an heir apparent.
According to the rules, the eldest son is always designated as the heir apparent.
However, Empress He’s actions, coupled with the downfall of General He Jin, have changed Emperor Ling’s mind.
More crucially, the eldest son, Liu Bian, was utterly incompetent—this was the most fatal flaw!
An emperor without talent isn’t inherently terrible, but one lacking courage and shrewdness will be unreliable; no one would dare entrust him with anything.
Being an emperor isn’t something just anyone can do.
Although Liu Hong was a scoundrel, he knew that if he passed the throne to his eldest son, Liu Bian, the Han dynasty, while not entirely destroyed, would at least be severely undermined.
Lu Ming’s words were much more direct; he didn’t care whether the Yuan family undermined the dynasty or not.
He had sent and placed countless people in Longxi Commandery. When he returned from Bingzhou, those who obeyed would be fine, but those who didn’t, he’d have them all chopped up!
Not a single one spared!

Jia Xu’s expression turned serious as he stroked his beard. "My lord, such slaughter, even if it stirs up bloodshed, is not to be feared, but we must be careful of a situation where we have no one to rely on."

"That’s alright," Lu Ming said, lowering his voice. "I have already learned of a method to improve paper. The paper produced is white, smooth, and suitable for writing. We will then copy all the books in Luoyang’s collection, and we will train our own scholars." He continued, "Back in the Chu-Han Contention, didn’t the King of Guanzhong rely on accumulating grain and delaying his declaration of kingship? We have plenty of time; three to five years is enough to train the necessary minor officials and civil servants."
Jia Xu and Fa Zheng were both shocked. Such a bold statement was practically tantamount to rebellion on their minds.

"The people suffer when the dynasty prospers, and the people suffer when it falls. If everyone in this world lived in peace and prosperity, the Yellow Turbans wouldn’t have rebelled. On their way here, did they see fields strewn with corpses? Powerful families monopolize power; to study, one must join their ranks. Power doesn’t last three generations; after three generations, chaos is inevitable. The Yuan and Yang families have held power for so many years. If they wanted, whether the empire would belong to the Liu or Yuan families is still uncertain!"

"Was the Yellow Turban Rebellion truly instigated by Zhang Jiao? The Yuan family played a significant role. Only when the Han dynasty collapsed did they have the opportunity and the qualifications to seize imperial power. With the people’s hearts corrupted, reverence naturally disappears. Heh, now in the border regions, Zhang Chun, the prefect of Zhongshan, has rebelled, Liaodong has responded, and together with the Wuhuan and Xianbei, they have launched a major uprising, raiding five prefectures: Qing, Xu, You, Ji, and Bing, killing and plundering officials and civilians, leaving devastation in their wake. Zhang Chun is a protégé of the Yuan family; without the Yuan family’s authorization and support, a mere prefect couldn’t have stirred up such a storm!"
This is a bit of a conspiracy theory, but regardless of whether it’s true or not, let’s first pin the blame on the Yuan family.
Lu Ming wanted to tell his two advisors his true thoughts on the world.
Putting oneself in others’ shoes is the only way to prepare a foolproof plan.
Jia Xu, abandoning his indifferent attitude, even became much more dignified in his kneeling posture.
His assessment was that of a ruthless strategist; with a single word, he tore away the last veil of shame from the Han dynasty.

"The Han Dynasty is on the verge of collapse. My lord, you are making thorough preparations. All the past events have enlightened me. Since you are so determined, why not recruit some talented individuals from among the wandering knights to act as your spies?"

"According to the strategy of stockpiling grain, it’s good, but we need someone to guard Longxi Commandery." Fa Zheng finally realized what was going on. Good heavens, this plot to rebel is truly outrageous!
However, he didn’t object, because in the eyes of a wise man, the Han Dynasty was already beyond saving.
Its reputation was almost completely ruined.
For decades, the buying and selling of official positions had caused widespread suffering.
Where did the money for buying official positions come from?
It was undoubtedly from extorting money from the people, which led to the Yellow Turban Rebellion.
It could be said that the Han Dynasty was rotten to the bone; even a god couldn’t save it.
Plus, there were powerful clans eyeing it covetously. Even if Bian Que (a legendary physician) came, he would only utter the three phrases: "It’s beyond saving," "It’s hopeless," and "Farewell."

As for the local powerful families, win them over if possible; those who cannot be won over will be killed. Their land and assets will be confiscated and placed in my name. We’ll recruit refugees and impoverished families to cultivate the land, prioritizing stable settlements." Scarcity increases value, and cities connecting the two regions will benefit greatly.

He also wanted to accomplish something, but he needed an opportunity and a ruler who could completely trust him.
Sending him elite soldiers to form a retinue wasn’t surveillance or suspicion, but rather a form of protection.
Longxi Commandery was devastated and ravaged, infiltrated by bandits and foreign tribes. Without any military power, going there would be tantamount to suicide.
This was no simple matter, but who was Jia Xu?
This problem was nothing to him.

Lu Ming disliked this kind of scholarly arrogance.
He rubbed his head.
"Wenhe, why not speak more bluntly?
I don’t understand."
Faced with such a direct and straightforward lord, Jia Xu was somewhat taken aback.
He thought about it and realized it made sense.
If the other party hadn’t been so direct and frank, he wouldn’t have switched allegiance to Lu Ming.
Even under Dong Zhuo, he had seen the man’s recklessness and pettiness; following Dong Zhuo wouldn’t lead to great things.

One is to send insignificant figures to provoke him, seeking weaknesses to convict him.
The other is to send envoys to Longxi County to undermine his power!"
This was something Lu Ming hadn’t considered.

There’s no need to worry about them being discarded after their usefulness is over.
Hmph, if the Yuan family doesn’t interfere, fine; but if they do, I’ll cut off their hands!
Wenhe, in terms of scheming and intrigue, I’m no match for the Yuan family, but often, not everything has to be done according to the rules."
The current emperor has not yet designated an heir apparent.
According to the rules, the eldest son is always designated as the heir apparent.

Not a single one spared!

Powerful families monopolize power; to study, one must join their ranks.

The Yuan and Yang families have held power for so many years.
If they wanted, whether the empire would belong to the Liu or Yuan families is still uncertain!"
"Was the Yellow Turban Rebellion truly instigated by Zhang Jiao?
The Yuan family played a significant role.
Only when the Han dynasty collapsed did they have the opportunity and the qualifications to seize imperial power.

chapters.title: Chapter 104 Yuan’s revenge
paragraphs: The Yuan family mansion, located in the north of the city, was a magnificent and extravagant palace. The main gate alone was five zhang wide, its vermilion doors and gilded plaques gleaming. Even the servants standing before the gate held their heads high, looking down on everyone.
In the main hall, Yuan Kui sat on a cushion, a cup of ginseng tea in his hand. "Benchu, how is the formation of the Western Garden Army progressing?"
Below him stood a handsome man with sword-like eyebrows, bright eyes, and a beard—Yuan Shao.
In terms of appearance, he was far more appealing than the somewhat gloomy Yuan Shu.
"Reporting to Uncle, five thousand men have been gathered. I have recruited the strongest men in Luoyang. With rigorous training, they will surely become an army!"
Seeing Yuan Shao’s smug expression, Yuan Shu, sitting below, felt a deep resentment.
His relationship with Yuan Shao was far from good; they maintained a facade of brotherly harmony, but in reality, he wished for Yuan Shao’s death.
The competition within powerful families was fierce, though not quite as intense as the struggle for succession, it wasn’t far off.
"Damn Yuan Shao! Hmph, you only got the position of Commandant of the Central Army because of compromise! What’s so smug about that!"
Bringing Yuan Shao in was a political compromise; getting two or three of the eight commanders of the Western Garden Army would be a feat.

If the Yuan family wanted to intervene, the Yang family would definitely intervene, and other families like the Wang family would also intervene. Emperor Ling also needed his own people; the eight positions were up for distribution.
Yuan Wei, however, wasn’t so pleased with Yuan Shao’s smugness. "How are the preparations going with the others?"
Although he didn’t say it, Yuan Wei most wanted to know about that little brat, Lu Ming.
He dared to set a trap for him in court!
That scene, that cunning consequence, even terrified him; this was cutting off the very foundation of the Yuan family!
Making the imperial family suspicious of the Yuan family was the greatest victory.

"Cao Cao has already recruited three thousand men, Chunyu Qiong has recruited two, and the other captains have each recruited one thousand." Yuan Shao paused, then added, "Lu Ming hasn’t recruited a single person yet."
"Hmph, drawing a salary from the court without doing any work, what will Jian Shuo say?" Yuan Wei scoffed. "Spread the word, make sure Lu Ming can’t recruit a single person!"
"Yes, Uncle." Yuan Shao’s impression of Lu Ming was so-so; he wasn’t particularly fond of him, nor did he dislike him, but who told him to offend his uncle?
As for what Lu Ming said in court, he had heard it, but found it laughable.
If powerful clans could be so easily defeated, they wouldn’t be powerful clans.
Yuan Shu didn’t speak, but instead pondered, "Uncle, why not recruit and subdue him as well?"
Upon hearing this, Yuan Shao’s lips twitched. His cousin seemed to know even the most basic facts.
Recruiting someone in this situation is impossible, given their already stated words.
Furthermore, the Yuan family no longer needs them. This person is clearly intended as a weapon against the Yuan family; how could they possibly be won over?

"Gonglu, working under the Minister of Justice, you can also cause trouble for Lu Ming there. Hmph, those who threaten the foundation of the Yuan family deserve to die!" Yuan Kui snorted. If it’s a matter of attitude, then it’s a matter of ability.
If he offends the Yuan family and doesn’t act, he’ll be looked down upon.
Powerful ministers, if they don’t use their power, they’re just asking for trouble.
"Yes, Uncle." Yuan Shu cursed inwardly, "Ignorant old man! Hmph! You want me to do this? I’ll just do it!"
The competition within the Yuan family is too fierce, and with an elder brother already ennobled, his rise to power is even more difficult.

Yuan Shao was once again dominating him. The other party was merely a bastard born of a concubine, yet he dared to ride roughshod over him. Yuan Shu, already narrow-minded, was now even more displeased.
Meanwhile, at Lu Ming’s residence.
Xu Shu arrived at the residence early in the morning with Jiang Qin and Zhou Tai. After being received, they saw his mother, who seemed much better. After a brief conversation, Lu Ming arrived.
"My lord, I am willing to serve you faithfully," Xu Shu said, clasping his hands in a fist salute. He was a filial son, and since Lu Ming had cured his mother, he should fulfill his promise.

"We are also willing to serve you, my lord," Zhou Tai and Jiang Qin said together, clasping their hands in a fist salute. This was undoubtedly a very good opportunity; if they missed it, no one might be willing to employ them in the future.
"Good, with these three, I am like a tiger with wings," Lu Ming laughed heartily, finally having recruited some historical generals.
"Yuanzhi, you should go to Yingchuan to study first. You have the brains, and I need you to return after your studies. You can also work for me, learning on the job. Think it over yourself."
Xu Shu replied solemnly, "I will go to Yingchuan to study and will definitely return in three years. During these three years, I entrust my mother to you, my lord!"
"Go and study. Your mother is with me; I will take good care of her." Lu Ming nodded, his face righteous and serious.
If Xu Shu knew that the other party had used him to blackmail his mother last night and then raped her, would he draw his sword?
That was utterly despicable!

"Yes, thank you, my lord." Xu Shu made up his mind to return after his studies and serve Lu Ming. He would repay kindness with kindness, just as a chivalrous knight repays debts of gratitude and avenges wrongs.
After settling Xu Shu, Lu Ming turned to look at Zhou Tai and Jiang Qin.

"I am the Prefect of Longxi Commandery, and I will have to return eventually. Youping, one of my advisors is returning to Longxi to handle government affairs for me; you will go with him. Your task this time is arduous; you must not only protect the Master’s safety but also organize troops to defend Longxi. After the rebellion, bandits roam the area, and the people are suffering. Are you willing to shoulder this heavy responsibility?" Lu Ming stared at Zhou Tai. Sending a southerner to Longxi seemed like leaving his homeland.

"Your subordinate is willing, my lord, do not worry. Anyone who wants to harm the Master will have to step over my dead body first," Zhou Tai said, clasping his hands in a fist salute, his tone resolute.
Even though it meant leaving his homeland, so what?
They had discussed this issue last night. Lu Ming certainly wouldn’t be limited to Longxi; he had a bright future ahead of him. Following such a lord, they could also rise through the ranks.

"Alright, I appoint you as the county’s bandit-hunting officer. You’ll have to put up with this for now. Once you arrive, you need to contact and recruit the local chivalrous heroes. They can achieve great things too." Lu Ming wasn’t stingy; he could still make decisions regarding personnel appointments within the county, it was within his power.

chapters.title: Chapter 105 Encountering harassment on the road
paragraphs: "Gongyi, you stay by my side and recruit wandering knights into my army, and discipline them strictly," Lu Ming said to Jiang Qin beside him. One would assist Jia Xu, while the other would stay and help him.
Both were former wandering knights, so recruiting them was relatively easy for them.
"Yes, my lord," Jiang Qin replied, inwardly excited. Following Lu Ming meant unexpected opportunities to achieve great things—this was a great opportunity!
After everything was arranged, Lu Ming went to the palace to treat Emperor Ling.
Only after finishing his work did he receive an imperial edict allowing him to go outside the city to recruit soldiers.
He could recruit as far as Hedong County outside Hangu Pass, as long as it wasn’t too far.
Everything was for convenience and to ensure success.
Leaving the palace, Lu Ming prepared to head to the South Market to recruit soldiers, but upon arriving, he heard a commotion.

"Go see what’s going on," Lu Ming said, looking at the chaos ahead. People were fleeing in panic, as if they had encountered something terrible. "Yes, my lord." Jiang Qin nimbly slipped into the crowd and disappeared in a flash.

Lu Ming felt a sense of foreboding, so he led his men to the side. A moment later, a squad of constables appeared from the street, gleaming broadswords at their waists, and walked directly towards him.
A resolute-faced man waved his hand, and the constables surrounded Lu Ming. "Are you Lu Ming?"
"I am Lu Ming, Prefect of Longxi Commandery and Colonel of the Western Garden Army. What? Are you here to arrest someone from the army?" Lu Ming flashed his token, a hint of mockery on his lips.
The man’s lips twitched slightly. He cursed inwardly, "You beast!" His superior had given him the task of bringing someone back to the yamen, and the person was just a colonel?
His initially tough attitude changed. "It’s my duty, please forgive me, sir."

"Since it’s my duty, then go back and tell the person who assigned you. The Xiyuan Army Captain is under the jurisdiction of the Upper Army Captain, and even the Grand General is subject to his command. Who do you think you are? Get out! Attacking the Xiyuan Army is tantamount to treason. Do you want to experience the taste of having your entire family exterminated?" Lu Ming threatened this brat without any politeness. He knew the Yuan family was not to be trifled with, but he didn’t expect them to be so blatantly causing him trouble!
"Heh, back to the yamen? Once you’re in, getting out won’t be so easy."
The man’s face turned ugly from the scolding. He wanted to say something, but dared not actually make a move.
The yamen runners could deal with ordinary people; they could arrest them at will, just by finding a reason.
But once they were in the yamen, how they were treated was up to them. However, dealing with someone from the military was not so simple. In essence, the yamen couldn’t interfere in military matters.
A short while later, Jiang Qin returned. He paused, surprised to see the constables, and approached them, saying, "My lord, it’s said that someone is harassing a woman and attacking her servants."
"Is that so?" Lu Ming stroked his chin. "Come on, follow me."
Seeing Lu Ming leave, a constable stepped forward and said, "Head constable, are we just going to let him go like that?"
*Slap!* The head constable slapped him, sending him spinning on the spot, seemingly venting his anger on his subordinate. "What can we do? Humph, come back with me to report!"
On South Street, a richly dressed young man had his retainers surround a carriage, a lewd smile playing on his lips.
These retainers were all battle-hardened soldiers; now that they were household guards, dealing with ordinary servants was like using a sledgehammer to crack a nut.
In no time, they had beaten the servants guarding the carriage to the ground!
"Young lady, come out, let this young master take a good look." The man dismounted and lifted the carriage curtain. The surrounding servants were all knocked to the ground; no one could stop him.
"Ah! You lecher!" A woman’s scream rang out, only making the man more excited.
"What a beautiful lady! Haha, today you’re mine!"
Lu Ming had just arrived when he witnessed this scene. He used to think that the rich would bully men and women, but in ancient times, this was commonplace.
The powerful could oppress the common people with impunity, and the common people couldn’t even resist.
"Tsk tsk tsk, who is this?"
"Who are you! Mind your own business!" Wu Ban saw someone younger than himself daring to interfere, so he snorted, not caring about the other person’s background.
Those who can make a living in Luoyang are mostly well-known figures. The playboys may not be serious, but that doesn’t mean they’re ignorant.
They know clearly who to mess with and who to avoid. So, seeing Lu Ming’s unfamiliar face, it’s obvious he’s an outsider.
There’s a saying among outsiders: even a powerful dragon can’t suppress a local snake. If you dare to step forward, you’d better know your place!
Lu Ming initially didn’t want to get involved, but a fleeting glance at the woman in the carriage caught his eye; she was quite beautiful.

Red lips, white teeth, stunningly beautiful face, a national treasure. Her pitiful appearance aroused an impulse in him to possess her. And for some reason, he felt this woman had a story, a woman he should know.
"Let her go. You can leave now, and nothing will happen." Lu Ming twisted his wrist. Since his sixth sense told him this girl had a story, he’d follow his intuition and investigate.
"Hahaha! You arrogant fool! Charge! Kill him! Don’t kill him!" Wu Ban was almost dying of laughter. His father was the General’s most trusted subordinate.
The General held immense power; even the Yuan family had to show him respect. Now, some nobody could mess with him? Wasn’t he courting death?
"Kill them all, spare his life. Spears in hand, follow me." Lu Ming pulled on his spear and launched a charge without warning.
His body leaned slightly forward, his steps steady, the spear concealed behind him—a standard concealed stance.

"Insolence! Die!" A swordsman wielding a longsword roared. One second his sword was still in its sheath, the next it was drawn, the blade aimed straight for Lu Ming’s throat. Clearly, he intended to kill him instantly—this wasn’t a fancy move, but a direct killing technique!

Clang! Spears clashed against swords, golden spears soaring high into the sky, radiating light like the sun and moon, their thrusts like a roaring dragon. In that single exchange, both sides knew the other was no easy opponent.

sentences.text: "Gongyi, you stay by my side and recruit wandering knights into my army, and discipline them strictly," Lu Ming said to Jiang Qin beside him.
One would assist Jia Xu, while the other would stay and help him.
Both were former wandering knights, so recruiting them was relatively easy for them.
"Yes, my lord," Jiang Qin replied, inwardly excited.
Following Lu Ming meant unexpected opportunities to achieve great things—this was a great opportunity!
After everything was arranged, Lu Ming went to the palace to treat Emperor Ling.
Only after finishing his work did he receive an imperial edict allowing him to go outside the city to recruit soldiers.
He could recruit as far as Hedong County outside Hangu Pass, as long as it wasn’t too far.
Everything was for convenience and to ensure success.
Leaving the palace, Lu Ming prepared to head to the South Market to recruit soldiers, but upon arriving, he heard a commotion.
"Go see what’s going on," Lu Ming said, looking at the chaos ahead.
People were fleeing in panic, as if they had encountered something terrible.
"Yes, my lord." Jiang Qin nimbly slipped into the crowd and disappeared in a flash.
Lu Ming felt a sense of foreboding, so he led his men to the side.
A moment later, a squad of constables appeared from the street, gleaming broadswords at their waists, and walked directly towards him.
A resolute-faced man waved his hand, and the constables surrounded Lu Ming.
"Are you Lu Ming?"
"I am Lu Ming, Prefect of Longxi Commandery and Colonel of the Western Garden Army.
What?
Are you here to arrest someone from the army?" Lu Ming flashed his token, a hint of mockery on his lips.
The man’s lips twitched slightly.
He cursed inwardly, "You beast!" His superior had given him the task of bringing someone back to the yamen, and the person was just a colonel?
His initially tough attitude changed.
"It’s my duty, please forgive me, sir."
"Since it’s my duty, then go back and tell the person who assigned you.
The Xiyuan Army Captain is under the jurisdiction of the Upper Army Captain, and even the Grand General is subject to his command.
Who do you think you are?
Get out!
Attacking the Xiyuan Army is tantamount to treason.
Do you want to experience the taste of having your entire family exterminated?" Lu Ming threatened this brat without any politeness.
He knew the Yuan family was not to be trifled with, but he didn’t expect them to be so blatantly causing him trouble!
"Heh, back to the yamen?
Once you’re in, getting out won’t be so easy."
The man’s face turned ugly from the scolding.
He wanted to say something, but dared not actually make a move.
The yamen runners could deal with ordinary people; they could arrest them at will, just by finding a reason.
But once they were in the yamen, how they were treated was up to them.
However, dealing with someone from the military was not so simple.
In essence, the yamen couldn’t interfere in military matters.
A short while later, Jiang Qin returned.
He paused, surprised to see the constables, and approached them, saying, "My lord, it’s said that someone is harassing a woman and attacking her servants."
"Is that so?" Lu Ming stroked his chin.
"Come on, follow me."
Seeing Lu Ming leave, a constable stepped forward and said, "Head constable, are we just going to let him go like that?"
*Slap!* The head constable slapped him, sending him spinning on the spot, seemingly venting his anger on his subordinate.
"What can we do?
Humph, come back with me to report!"
On South Street, a richly dressed young man had his retainers surround a carriage, a lewd smile playing on his lips.
These retainers were all battle-hardened soldiers; now that they were household guards, dealing with ordinary servants was like using a sledgehammer to crack a nut.
In no time, they had beaten the servants guarding the carriage to the ground!
"Young lady, come out, let this young master take a good look." The man dismounted and lifted the carriage curtain.
The surrounding servants were all knocked to the ground; no one could stop him.
"Ah!
You lecher!" A woman’s scream rang out, only making the man more excited.
"What a beautiful lady!
Haha, today you’re mine!"
Lu Ming had just arrived when he witnessed this scene.
He used to think that the rich would bully men and women, but in ancient times, this was commonplace.
The powerful could oppress the common people with impunity, and the common people couldn’t even resist.
"Tsk tsk tsk, who is this?"
"Who are you!
Mind your own business!" Wu Ban saw someone younger than himself daring to interfere, so he snorted, not caring about the other person’s background.
Those who can make a living in Luoyang are mostly well-known figures.
The playboys may not be serious, but that doesn’t mean they’re ignorant.
They know clearly who to mess with and who to avoid.
So, seeing Lu Ming’s unfamiliar face, it’s obvious he’s an outsider.
There’s a saying among outsiders: even a powerful dragon can’t suppress a local snake.
If you dare to step forward, you’d better know your place!
Lu Ming initially didn’t want to get involved, but a fleeting glance at the woman in the carriage caught his eye; she was quite beautiful.
Red lips, white teeth, stunningly beautiful face, a national treasure.
Her pitiful appearance aroused an impulse in him to possess her.
And for some reason, he felt this woman had a story, a woman he should know.
"Let her go.
You can leave now, and nothing will happen." Lu Ming twisted his wrist.
Since his sixth sense told him this girl had a story, he’d follow his intuition and investigate.
"Hahaha!
You arrogant fool!
Charge!
Kill him!
Don’t kill him!" Wu Ban was almost dying of laughter.
His father was the General’s most trusted subordinate.
The General held immense power; even the Yuan family had to show him respect.
Now, some nobody could mess with him?
Wasn’t he courting death?
"Kill them all, spare his life.
Spears in hand, follow me." Lu Ming pulled on his spear and launched a charge without warning.
His body leaned slightly forward, his steps steady, the spear concealed behind him—a standard concealed stance.
"Insolence!
Die!" A swordsman wielding a longsword roared.
One second his sword was still in its sheath, the next it was drawn, the blade aimed straight for Lu Ming’s throat.
Clearly, he intended to kill him instantly—this wasn’t a fancy move, but a direct killing technique!
Clang!
Spears clashed against swords, golden spears soaring high into the sky, radiating light like the sun and moon, their thrusts like a roaring dragon.
In that single exchange, both sides knew the other was no easy opponent.

chapters.title: Chapter 106 Yuan Shu and Yuan Gonglu
paragraphs: *Thud!* Lu Ming twisted his spear, causing it to spin, and then unleashed a series of thrusts to the left and right!
*Thud!*
*Thud!*
With two consecutive spear flourishes, the two guards collapsed to the ground, and the thrusts forced the swordsman to reposition himself.
Longsword against spear, an inch longer, an inch stronger; years of practice with the sword and staff, years of honing the spear, a treasured sword always at hand.
Sword and spear are the most difficult to master; constant practice is essential to maintain a feel for the weapon.
Wang Ci felt immense pressure. He was the nephew of the swordsman Wang Yue, currently serving under the Grand General, and assigned to protect Wu Ban.
He had always been successful, even somewhat complacent. His swordsmanship wasn’t bad, but encountering a master caught him off guard.
Moreover, the pressure Lu Ming exerted was a killing pressure, not just flashy moves, but techniques capable of killing silently at any moment.
The other followers swarmed forward, seemingly chaotic, yet maintaining formation.
They formed groups of three, back to back, one defending, one attacking, and one supporting, executing the three-on-three system flawlessly.

Wu Ban’s guards were utterly powerless to resist. They were veterans, yes, but facing veterans who had also fought their way through mountains of corpses and seas of blood, who had followed Lu Ming in charging and beheading thousands of rebel soldiers, and who possessed professional buffs, they were no match. They were slaughtered in a single round!
From the outbreak of the riot to its suppression, only a dozen or so breaths had passed.
More than twenty guards were wiped out, leaving only Wang Ci desperately parrying.
Thud!
Lu Ming feigned a spear flourish, tricking Wang Ci into parrying.
Lu Ming rapidly spun the spearhead and slammed it down.
Wang Ci’s instincts kicked in; at the crucial moment, he turned his body, but his right hand had already been pierced!
A piercing pain shot through him, before he could even scream.

Lu Ming forcefully flicked the end of the spear, using its elasticity and rotation to further amplify its power, bringing the spearhead to the destructive force of the Overlord Spear—an extraordinary burst of energy.
*Thud!*
Wang Ci’s entire arm was shattered by the immense force, and he collapsed to the ground screaming in agony.
This wasn’t just a severed arm; it was a comminuted fracture!
Even in modern times, this would be difficult to heal, let alone in ancient times; it would essentially result in permanent disability!
And with the bleeding continuing, it could very well be fatal!
Just as Lu Ming was about to finish off the man, a middle-aged burly man ran up and shouted, "My lord, spare him!"
Upon seeing the man, Wu Ban was terrified, but then became smug again, shouting, "Shi A, kill him! Kill him quickly!"

Despite rushing, Shi A was still a step too late. Seeing Wang Ci’s shattered right arm, he gasped, "My lord, I am Shi A, a disciple of General Wang Yue, the Tiger General under the Grand General. This is Wu Ban, son of General Wu Huwei. Please, my lord, spare him."

"Hmm, you can take him away. Tell Wu Ban that today’s events were his son’s own doing. Attacking a captain of the Western Garden Army, heh, His Majesty’s personal guard. If you’re not satisfied, go ahead and complain to the Emperor. I’ll see it through!" Lu Ming asserted his authority, even though a captain wasn’t much.

However, the Western Garden Army, newly established by Emperor Ling, was at the height of its power. To attack the Western Garden Army at this time was tantamount to slapping Emperor Ling in the face!
"Don’t hit someone in the face, especially the emperor’s face! That’s practically suicide!"
"Understood," Shi A replied, then left with Wang Ci and Wu Ban.
He had witnessed Lu Ming’s skills from afar. They were incredibly formidable; every move was deadly, not just for show. He had only ever seen such power in his master, Wang Yue.
But his master was no longer young. Youth has its advantages; the younger generation is truly formidable!
"Let me go, you bastard! Lu Ming, right? You just wait!" Wu Ban wasn’t stupid either. Pulled along by Shi A, he shouted a couple of times in a show of bravado before leaving.
He’d utter those threats; there would be plenty of time to get his revenge.
Lu Ming didn’t take it seriously. These spoiled brats relied solely on their fathers’ influence. If they were truly successful, they wouldn’t be acting like spoiled brats here.
"Girl, it’s alright. Your servants have all been killed. Where do you live? I’ll take you home."
"Thank you, sir. My father is Colonel Feng Fang. Please take me home." Feng Fangnu forced herself to remain calm and bowed deeply to Lu Ming.
At this moment, Feng Fangnu’s portrait appeared on the character panel. Clicking on it revealed her skills, talents, stats, age, and introduction.
Feng Qin (Feng Fangnu), a beauty of unparalleled grace. During Dong Zhuo’s chaos, Feng Fangnu sought refuge in Yangzhou.
Yuan Shu saw her when he ascended the city walls, was delighted, and took her as his wife, showering her with affection.
Later, due to the jealousy of Yuan Shu’s wives and concubines, they strangled her and hung her body from a beam in the latrine, claiming that Feng Fangnu had committed suicide out of resentment.
Yuan Shu indeed believed she had died of frustration and despair, and thus gave her a grand funeral.
Looking at the character’s profile, Lu Ming had a thought he shouldn’t have!
This was Yuan Shu’s wife, not yet, but now that he’d encountered her, could he just stand by and do nothing?
So beautiful, so pitiful, especially the golden tassels in her hair, complementing her exquisite face and fair skin—easily arousing a man’s desire.
Wasn’t his goal to have his way with all the beauties in the world, with the wives, daughters, and mothers of all the warlords and heroes?
Now, a perfect opportunity presented itself; why let it slip by?
"No problem, I’ll take you back," Lu Ming said to his personal guard. "Come with me in the carriage."
In the distance, the constables who had previously left returned, this time led by Yuan Shu.
He hadn’t originally planned to come; he had his own reasons.
A servant had just reported a vicious fight and murder at the market, involving Lu Ming again, which was why he’d come.
Lu Ming spotted him from afar: a man with a gloomy face but dressed in fine clothes. "May I ask which lord you are?"
"I am Yuan Shu, the Minister of Justice, Yuan Gonglu," Yuan Shu introduced himself. The Minister of Justice was a position responsible for trials.
They also had the duty of apprehending criminals; they could handle anything related to crime.

"So you are the extraordinary man of Luoyang, the foremost member of the Yuan family, Yuan Gonglu! Brother Gonglu, I’ve long admired you. Back in Xiliang, I often heard of your great name, your public-spiritedness, your respect for the virtuous, known as the Timely Rain Yuan Gonglu. Seeing you today, I can confirm it. I’m truly impressed." Lu Ming showered him with flattery. If he hadn’t witnessed it firsthand, he wouldn’t have known that a skilled and valiant general could flatter so fluently, without even realizing it.

chapters.title: Chapter 107 Cooperation benefits both sides
paragraphs: Feng Qin peeked curiously at Lu Ming from outside the carriage. Lu Ming was young and handsome, and he had saved her.
If Lu Ming hadn’t appeared, she probably would have been taken away by Wu Ban and forcibly violated!
Although her father was one of the Eight Colonels of the Western Garden, he was now merely clinging to life, his power far diminished.
Otherwise, Wu Ban wouldn’t have dared to bully her; he only did so because of her family’s decline, intending to force himself on her.
Feng Fang was the son-in-law of the eunuch Cao Jie, and eunuchs were inherently disliked.
Being the son-in-law of a eunuch meant being part of the eunuch faction—an inescapable label, destined to be disliked.
Cao Jie was long dead, so Feng Fang had lost his support, which was why Emperor Ling used him.
Disliked and ostracized by scholars, he had no choice but to rely on the emperor, or resign and retire to his hometown—but was that even possible?

Yuan Shu, flattered by the flattery, relaxed considerably, his previously gloomy expression brightening considerably. He smiled and cupped his hands, saying, "You’re too kind, Brother Anmin. Brother Anmin, did you kill someone in the South Market?"

"It was merely a rebellious act by some traitors who attacked His Majesty’s personal guards, tantamount to treason. I will personally go to the palace tomorrow to report the matter to His Majesty and request His Majesty’s judgment. Brother Gonglu, do not worry, I will not make things difficult for you." Lu Ming then leaned closer and said, "Wu Ban’s actions are suspected of treason. Why don’t you investigate further, Brother Gonglu? It might be a great achievement. If this succeeds, Brother Gonglu’s reputation will not only spread in Luoyang, but throughout the Central Plains and Hebei!"
This was indeed a very good suggestion. Yuan Shu had great ambition, but lacked the talent for action.

Those who left their mark on the Three Kingdoms were not fools or idiots. He was indeed going to make things difficult for Lu Ming, but if cooperating with Lu Ming could bring him benefits, then why not? At this time, Yuan Shu’s elder brother, Yuan Ji, was still alive and hadn’t yet been beheaded by Dong Zhuo. He was still under pressure, and although he could rely on the Yuan family’s reputation to attract talent, it was ultimately limited.
After a brief moment of thought, Yuan Shu let Lu Ming go, clasping his hands in a fist salute, "Brother Anmin, please feel free. I will go to the General’s residence to investigate this matter."
After a pause, Yuan Shu asked in a low voice, "It is rumored that Brother Anmin is a reincarnation of a divine physician, capable of reviving the dead and restoring flesh to bones. Is this true?"

"Brother Gonglu, you flatter me. I do possess medical skills, but I cannot revive the dead. Brother Gonglu, if you need anything, please don’t hesitate to ask. We hit it off immediately, and it’s time for us to work together." Lu Ming offered a slight show of humility, then emphasized that he would treat patients, but only if the benefits were substantial.
"Alright, this matter is not urgent. After this matter is settled, I will invite Brother Anmin to my residence for a drink." Yuan Shu said, cupping his hands and gesturing for his men to make way.
The world is a bustling place, driven by self-interest; there are no permanent enemies, only permanent interests.
Lu Ming had offended Yuan Wei, Yuan Shu’s uncle, but what did that have to do with Yuan Shu?
As long as it benefited him, he could use it.

Otherwise, if he did nothing, Yuan Shao would steal all the limelight, and with his brother Yuan Ji becoming his uncle, it would be even harder for him to rise. Better to be a big fish in a small pond than a small fish in a big pond; Yuan Shu was unwilling to be subservient.
Having passed through smoothly, Lu Ming breathed a sigh of relief. This was fortunate to have encountered Yuan Shu.
He could communicate with him using words; otherwise, if he had encountered someone else, it might have come to blows.
He wasn’t afraid of these things, but indiscriminate killing would still have negative consequences and wouldn’t benefit him.
This also gave him a deeper impression and understanding of these powerful figures. Historical figures?
They were all just human. Since they were human, they had interests, and the exchange of interests was always the most effective.
After Lu Ming left, Yuan Shu sent men to collect the corpses and weapons left in the market; they would surely be useful.
Dealing with Wu Kuang was dealing with the Grand General, and also with Yuan Shao. The Grand General favored the Yuan family, so this was essentially fighting among themselves.
But did it matter?
What did it matter to Yuan Shu if the Yuan family benefited?
Everyone looks out for themselves!

The journey was silent. Lu Ming escorted Feng Qin to Feng Fang’s residence, cupping his hands in a fist salute. "Miss, if possible, tell Lord Feng about this. This might be aimed at him, and you are merely a trigger. Don’t go out recently. If there are any problems, you can contact me."
"Thank you, sir. I will write a letter and send someone to inform my father." Feng Qin bowed gracefully, her heart filled with goodwill towards Lu Ming.
This young man—marrying him would be a wonderful thing!
Thinking of this, she blushed slightly. It’s perfectly normal for a young girl to have feelings of first love, unlike students who see many boys of similar age, so their mindset is different.
Lu Ming didn’t linger, but instead headed straight for Zhao Hou’s residence.
Someone was bound to cause trouble today, so he needed to prepare early to avoid being caught off guard.
He wasn’t very good at this kind of scheming. Knowing his personality, he would simply eliminate them all, ending it all. He didn’t need any social niceties.
Social niceties were only necessary when one lacked strength. With enough strength, it was all about crushing the enemy; there was no need for favors!
Upon arriving at Zhao Hou’s residence, Zhao Hou hadn’t returned yet. Lu Ming decided to wait, intending to deal with it after Zhao Hou’s return.
"Are you Lu Ming?" A slick-haired, well-groomed man entered. He was good-looking, but his steps were unsteady, his face pale, and his dark circles were very noticeable.
It was easy to see that this was a spoiled brat, living a life of extravagance and irregular habits, his body completely drained!
"My name is Liu Zan. I’ve heard your medical skills are excellent? Take a look at me, see what’s wrong with me." Liu Zan’s tone was very impolite, as if he were ordering a servant.
"This captain is here to discuss matters with Marquis Zhao. If you want treatment, you’ll have to make an appointment." Lu Ming frowned, clearly disliking the other man’s attitude.
Bang! Liu Zan slammed his hand on the table, pointing at Lu Ming’s nose and cursing, "You’re nothing but a dog of the Liu family, how dare you disobey me!"
"Heh, is this your own idea?" Lu Ming laughed angrily. This kind of person was really asking for death.
Was it because of his privileged upbringing?
Compared to the Yuan family, he was indeed far inferior. Even Yuan Shu, who was known for his strategic acumen but lack of talent, was many times better than him.
The decline of noble families and the rise of powerful clans are not without reason.

We hit it off immediately, and it’s time for us to work together." Lu Ming offered a slight show of humility, then emphasized that he would treat patients, but only if the benefits were substantial.
"Alright, this matter is not urgent.
After this matter is settled, I will invite Brother Anmin to my residence for a drink." Yuan Shu said, cupping his hands and gesturing for his men to make way.
The world is a bustling place, driven by self-interest; there are no permanent enemies, only permanent interests.
Lu Ming had offended Yuan Wei, Yuan Shu’s uncle, but what did that have to do with Yuan Shu?
As long as it benefited him, he could use it.
Otherwise, if he did nothing, Yuan Shao would steal all the limelight, and with his brother Yuan Ji becoming his uncle, it would be even harder for him to rise.
Better to be a big fish in a small pond than a small fish in a big pond; Yuan Shu was unwilling to be subservient.
Having passed through smoothly, Lu Ming breathed a sigh of relief.
This was fortunate to have encountered Yuan Shu.
He could communicate with him using words; otherwise, if he had encountered someone else, it might have come to blows.
He wasn’t afraid of these things, but indiscriminate killing would still have negative consequences and wouldn’t benefit him.
This also gave him a deeper impression and understanding of these powerful figures.
Historical figures?
They were all just human.
Since they were human, they had interests, and the exchange of interests was always the most effective.
After Lu Ming left, Yuan Shu sent men to collect the corpses and weapons left in the market; they would surely be useful.
Dealing with Wu Kuang was dealing with the Grand General, and also with Yuan Shao.
The Grand General favored the Yuan family, so this was essentially fighting among themselves.
But did it matter?
What did it matter to Yuan Shu if the Yuan family benefited?
Everyone looks out for themselves!
The journey was silent.
Lu Ming escorted Feng Qin to Feng Fang’s residence, cupping his hands in a fist salute.
"Miss, if possible, tell Lord Feng about this.
This might be aimed at him, and you are merely a trigger.
Don’t go out recently.
If there are any problems, you can contact me."
"Thank you, sir.
I will write a letter and send someone to inform my father." Feng Qin bowed gracefully, her heart filled with goodwill towards Lu Ming.
This young man—marrying him would be a wonderful thing!
Thinking of this, she blushed slightly.
It’s perfectly normal for a young girl to have feelings of first love, unlike students who see many boys of similar age, so their mindset is different.
Lu Ming didn’t linger, but instead headed straight for Zhao Hou’s residence.
Someone was bound to cause trouble today, so he needed to prepare early to avoid being caught off guard.
He wasn’t very good at this kind of scheming.
Knowing his personality, he would simply eliminate them all, ending it all.
He didn’t need any social niceties.
Social niceties were only necessary when one lacked strength.
With enough strength, it was all about crushing the enemy; there was no need for favors!
Upon arriving at Zhao Hou’s residence, Zhao Hou hadn’t returned yet.
Lu Ming decided to wait, intending to deal with it after Zhao Hou’s return.
"Are you Lu Ming?" A slick-haired, well-groomed man entered.
He was good-looking, but his steps were unsteady, his face pale, and his dark circles were very noticeable.
It was easy to see that this was a spoiled brat, living a life of extravagance and irregular habits, his body completely drained!
"My name is Liu Zan.
I’ve heard your medical skills are excellent?
Take a look at me, see what’s wrong with me." Liu Zan’s tone was very impolite, as if he were ordering a servant.
"This captain is here to discuss matters with Marquis Zhao.
If you want treatment, you’ll have to make an appointment." Lu Ming frowned, clearly disliking the other man’s attitude.
Bang!
Liu Zan slammed his hand on the table, pointing at Lu Ming’s nose and cursing, "You’re nothing but a dog of the Liu family, how dare you disobey me!"
"Heh, is this your own idea?" Lu Ming laughed angrily.
This kind of person was really asking for death.
Was it because of his privileged upbringing?
Compared to the Yuan family, he was indeed far inferior.
Even Yuan Shu, who was known for his strategic acumen but lack of talent, was many times better than him.
The decline of noble families and the rise of powerful clans are not without reason.

chapters.title: Chapter 108 Accuse first
paragraphs: "What! You dog, you’re not happy about this?! You dare talk back! I’ll beat you up!" Liu Zan seemed to have lost his mind, completely unaware of Lu Ming’s importance to Marquis Zhao.
He thought that being the eldest son guaranteed him the title, little did he know that such a good-for-nothing was exactly what powerful families wanted.
They had status, but no ability; they could be manipulated at will and made to obey.
Especially status and influence—easy to use and control. Where else could they find such a thing?
Lu Ming chuckled, grabbed Liu Zan’s arm, and shoved him to the ground. "You’re drunk, I won’t stoop to your level."
"You slave, you dare to resist!" Liu Zan, bracing himself on his arms, straddled the ground, looking somewhat disheveled and furious.
He stood up, baring his teeth and claws, ready to pounce. Where did he get his confidence? Did he think he was something special?

Lady Wang Qing, wife of Marquis Zhao, rushed in from outside. Upon entering, she saw her eldest son punching and kicking Lu Ming, and felt a surge of shame and anger, her face burning with embarrassment.
"Stop! Zan’er, what are you doing!"
"Mother! This dog of a servant dares to defy me! I’ll beat him to death!" Liu Zan, seeing his mother arrive, became even more energetic, completely unaware that he was being manipulated.
Lu Ming grabbed Liu Zan by the collar with one hand and lifted him up. "I admire Marquis Zhao, not you. What right do you have to speak ill of me!"

"Anmin, don’t do it!" Wang Qing felt a sudden rush of panic and a wave of dizziness washed over her. If it weren’t for the maid behind her supporting her, she probably would have collapsed to the ground.
"Thump!" Lu Ming threw Liu Zan to the ground like a dog, coldly sneering, "Since Madam says so, of course I will do as she says."

"You!" Liu Zan was furious, standing up again to attack Lu Ming. Just then, Zhao Hou returned. Seeing his eldest son’s appearance, he immediately snorted coldly, "Nonsense! Zan’er, what are you doing!"

"Father, you’re back just in time. That dog of a servant! I wanted him to take a look at me, to see what’s wrong with me. Isn’t he a doctor? But he refused! That dog of a servant!" Liu Zan thought he was right. If it were an ordinary doctor, they would have reluctantly examined him, and if they didn’t want to treat him, they would have said everything was fine, nothing serious, just plenty of rest, and other such nonsense.
But Lu Ming wouldn’t tolerate him. His attitude was terrible, and he even called him a dog!
Ha! This is the hypocrisy of royalty. No matter how hard the people below work, in their eyes, they’re nothing but dogs!
Thinking of this, he became extremely angry. Indeed, status and position aren’t so easily changed.
"Nonsense! Go back and reflect on your actions! Get out!" The Marquis’s face was ashen. His good-for-nothing son still reeked of alcohol; he’d drunkenly gone mad!
"Guards, take him away!"
Several guards came and dragged the drunken Liu Zan away. What did it matter if he was facing the eldest son? It was the Marquis’s order anyway.
The Marquis took the main seat. A maidservant brought him fragrant tea. He slowly took a sip. "Anmin, sit. My son’s drunken outburst, please don’t take offense."

"Marquis, you flatter me. A drunk person doesn’t remember what they did and is out of control. Just take it as a joke." Lu Ming smiled on the surface, but inwardly he was cursing the other man’s ancestors.
He’s a dog?
Then don’t blame him for being impolite.
"Your Majesty, is there something important that brings you here at this hour, Anmin?" The Marquis didn’t bother to explain; he was already being generous by saying even a single word.
The powerful must maintain their status, but a proper reprimand can also make Lu Ming realize his place.
Lu Ming recounted his encounter with Wu Ban. Since a murder had occurred in the street, this matter needed to be clarified.
After listening, Zhao Hou narrowed his eyes. Instead of questioning Lu Ming’s purpose in going to the market, he asked, "How do you plan to deal with them?"
"First, establish their crimes: attacking the Emperor’s personal guards, plotting rebellion!" Lu Ming’s voice was firm, indicating his certainty.
Either do it at all, or do it decisively, leaving no regrets.

"Wu Kuang is a trusted confidant of the Grand General. Wouldn’t you be offending the Grand General in this way?" Zhao Hou’s expression was ambiguous, neither a warning nor a schadenfreude, leaving one unsure whether he was truly admonishing Lu Ming, observing the situation, or both.

"I am His Majesty’s subject, and my loyalty is also to His Majesty. What does it matter to the Grand General? As fellow ministers, if I act uprightly, I have nothing to fear. The Western Garden Army has only just been formed, and Wu Kuang has already committed such despicable acts; there must be some conspiracy involved," Lu Ming said in a low voice, narrowing his eyes. "With the Empress Dowager’s relatives and the Yuan family allied, even Marquis Zhao might have to act according to their wishes."
These words struck a chord with him. A man like him, adept at navigating both sides, detested any single force being absolutely dominant.
His loyalty to the Emperor was his duty, and it didn’t matter to him who won.
However, when one side held too much power, mere flattery and song were useless.
"Come with me to the palace to meet the Emperor," Marquis Zhao said after a moment’s thought, offering a decisive analysis.

Even in that brief moment, many possibilities flashed through his mind. If Empress He’s son were to become Emperor in the future, wouldn’t the Grand General and the Yuan family cause chaos? Moreover, his relationship with He Jin wasn’t exactly good.
In ancient times, the presumption of guilt depended on who saw the emperor first. Under similar conditions, whoever could win the emperor’s favor first would win.

While Wu Kuang was still gritting his teeth, preparing to report to General He Jin after witnessing his son Wu Ban’s ordeal, Zhao Hou and Lu Ming had already arrived at the palace and begun their complaint.
Yangxin Hall, Mingde Palace.
Emperor Ling, Liu Hong, having just dismounted from a woman, received Lu Ming and Zhao Hou in loose clothing.
After listening to their account, he narrowed his eyes. "So, it’s the General targeting the Western Garden Army?"

"I wouldn’t say for sure, but it’s possible that some of the General’s retainers have objections. After all, even the General, who commands all the armies in the land, is subject to the control of the Upper Army Commandant; it’s impossible for him not to have objections." Lu Ming preemptively pinned the blame on them. Whether it was true or not, it would at least cause some trouble for He Jin.

chapters.title: Chapter 109 Zhang Rang’s transaction
paragraphs: "Anmin, what are your thoughts?" Emperor Ling squinted, appearing somewhat drowsy.
Men always feel tired after sex.
When young, they can have sex multiple times a day, but as they age, their libido declines, and their energy wanes. Women, on the other hand, experience the opposite.

"Your Majesty, I’ll give you acupuncture first. After some time, I might try to recreate the ancient formula. It’s more effective than current aphrodisiacs and can prolong ejaculation, extending it from a quarter of an hour to three quarters of an hour." Lu Ming catered to Emperor Ling’s desires. Since Emperor Ling enjoyed women but lacked the stamina, he could easily address this issue.
"Oh? Do you have such an ancient formula?" Emperor Ling was slightly excited. Besides amassing wealth, he also indulged in women.
Although frequent encounters with women weren’t ideal, how could he resist a thousand beautiful women?
No man could resist; it required immense self-control.

"I’d seen it before, but never studied it in depth. I only recently had the urge to research and recreate it, but unfortunately, the prescription is too incomplete. Restoring even half of its effects would be the best I could hope for. Otherwise, according to the ancient prescription, it could at least make a man’s penis as hard as iron, lasting an hour without a problem," Lu Ming continued to boast. This was something no man could resist.
Ancient aphrodisiacs were packaged in a small box containing neatly arranged small round balls, each wrapped in oiled paper. He took out two, unwrapped the paper, and inside were black, round pills.

While studying traditional Chinese medicine in this era, Lu Ming naturally discovered many shortcomings in its theories. Modern medical theory was far more advanced than that of traditional Chinese medicine. Lu Ming also came across some theories of aphrodisiac concoctions from traditional sexual practices. These theories were utterly naive and laughable. Ancient Chinese medicine emphasized the combination of Yin and Yang, the unity of the Five Elements, and the interaction of Qi, form, and spirit. Many aphrodisiacs made based on these principles went astray.

Lu Ming scoffed at these homemade aphrodisiacs. They contained few active ingredients and were highly harmful to the body. In ancient times, many powerful figures died from "excessive indulgence," but these deaths weren’t actually due to exhaustion; most were caused by overuse of aphrodisiacs.
"Good, good, good, Anmin! Once you’ve finished, come directly to the palace to see me." Emperor Ling was overjoyed. An aphrodisiac that could prolong ejaculation was a great thing.
He loved this; he enjoyed playing with women, but his body wouldn’t allow it.
The pleasure of sex was great for men, but not necessarily for women.
"Go ahead and do it. I’ll take care of everything. Rangfu, you’re in charge of this."
The old eunuch Zhang Rang, who had been standing nearby, beamed. "Yes, Your Majesty! This old servant will handle it perfectly."
Seeing Lu Ming’s imperial favor, a flicker of hesitation crossed Zhao Hou’s mind.
"Let’s wait and see. The Yuan family has only just made their move; they definitely won’t let Lu Ming get away so easily."
As for his eldest son Liu Zan’s nonsense, he agreed with it in his heart, but couldn’t say it aloud.
"Some things can’t be said, only done; some things can only be said, not done. Clearly, his rebellious son doesn’t understand this principle at all!"
"There’s no need for excessive complexity; just a little bit of catering to his preferences will suffice. Emperor Ling may not be a good emperor, but he’s definitely a very useful tool."
"After the treatment, the palace gates were already closed; leaving the palace was impossible. He had to stay overnight, which was an immense blessing for an ordinary person."
"Zhao Hou has obviously done this more than once or twice; he was taken to rest by palace maids. Only Lu Ming continued treating Emperor Ling, and even prepared some food for a late-night snack."
"Only those who have experienced it understand its preciousness."
Emperor Ling was growing increasingly fond of Lu Ming. He was a master of both military conquest and domestic medicine, a true all-rounder.
Furthermore, after a simple acupuncture treatment, Emperor Ling felt a long-lost surge of virility. He immediately summoned a maid and had her perform acupuncture in front of Lu Ming.

Zhang Rang watched from the side. As a eunuch, watching wouldn’t hurt, and Emperor Ling was clearly used to it. Lu Ming, however, felt somewhat embarrassed and uncomfortable, and could only lower his head to drink and eat his late-night snack.
"Lord Lu, His Majesty treats you like one of his own. Even Marquis Zhao doesn’t receive this treatment," Zhang Rang whispered, his tone seemingly ingratiating and flattering.
His power stemmed from Emperor Ling. Once Emperor Ling died, he would be no different from a stray dog.
Having wielded immense power for over thirty years, he was unwilling to relinquish it and would do everything in his power to prolong its life.

"As a subject, one should naturally learn both literary and martial arts, and serve the Emperor," Lu Ming smiled, glancing at Zhang Rang. "Zhang Gong, you look quite well, your breathing is steady, and your eyes are bright and alert. You’ll live to be at least ninety years old."
Ninety years old is practically impossible in ancient times. A long-lived elder held a very high status; at least at seventy, Han law stipulated that one could refuse to bow to officials.
If someone else said this, it might be considered a compliment, but coming from Lu Ming, it was an absolute affirmation.
Zhang Rang was overjoyed, laughing, "Lord Lu, you’re joking!"
"Zhang Gong, please just call me Anmin. ’Lord’ is too formal," Lu Ming laughed heartily. Was dealing with eunuchs shameful? It was as if he gained something by not dealing with them.
"Since that’s the case, I’ll gladly accept your offer." Zhang Rang gave a forced smile; the eunuch’s gloom always made one uncomfortable. "I will personally arrange accommodations for Anmin later."
"Then I’ll trouble you, Master Zhang." Lu Ming didn’t stand on ceremony; at least he could sense that the guards here were all quite capable.

"No problem. If Anmin has time, perhaps you could examine my adopted son, Zhang Feng. He’s my only adopted son, and he’s recently contracted tuberculosis. If possible, please do your best to treat him." Zhang Rang’s expression was sincere; it was clear that eunuchs valued their adopted sons highly.
Even adopted sons were treated like biological sons, simply because eunuchs couldn’t have children.
One was a source of longing, the other a source of hope; at least there was an heir. Even if he retired to his hometown in the future, at least someone would be there to see him off.

chapters.title: Chapter 110 Staying overnight at the palace
paragraphs: Clearly, this was a deal.
If Lu Ming cured Zhang Rang’s adopted son, Zhang Rang would use Emperor Ling’s influence to help Lu Ming suppress Wu Ban’s affair.
This kind of thing could be big or small, entirely depending on whether he wanted to manipulate it.
A pawn can only gain a sliver of initiative and sufficient benefit by maximizing its role, thus potentially becoming the player in the game.

"That’s alright, but the medicinal herbs are rather difficult to find. I’ll try to find some time tomorrow. This matter isn’t certain, and I can’t guarantee it," Lu Ming said, his brows furrowed, appearing unusually serious.
This actually reassured Zhang Rang considerably. If Lu Ming had guaranteed a cure, he would have been more skeptical.
Having seen too many boastful people, he found it surprisingly pleasant to be around such an honest person.
The two discussed various matters, which Emperor Ling overheard, but he ignored it, preoccupied with his affairs with the palace maid.
He shivered slightly, then stopped, and soon fell fast asleep.
The palace maid beneath him, blushing, got up and dressed, still needing to attend to Emperor Ling as he lay down.
"Anmin, please come with me," Zhang Rang said, after covering Emperor Ling with a blanket, and personally led a group to find a side hall for Lu Ming to sleep in.
It was Lu Ming’s first time staying overnight in the palace, and he still found it quite novel.
He was unaware that Yuan Shi and Yang Shi already knew, and were beginning to waver.
Being able to stay overnight in the palace at least proved the other person’s ability and their position in the emperor’s heart.
Originally, they thought Lu Ming would be neglected after his unpleasant encounter with the eldest son of the Marquis of Zhao, but now it seemed they had worried too much.
Yuan Kui was about to go to sleep, but after receiving the news, he found himself unable to sleep.
He hadn’t expected that Lu Ming, whom he considered a little beast, could reach this point; now, dealing with him was proving difficult.
But letting him swallow this insult was absolutely out of the question; the thought of it was making him increasingly enraged!
On the other hand, the Yang family’s attitude was somewhat ambiguous, remaining neutral, watching the drama unfold from the sidelines.
Who won or lost was of no consequence to them.
And the influence Lu Ming had displayed might just entice the Yang family to invest a little.

Actually, this so-called side hall was merely a slightly larger room than a regular one. There were still palace maids serving him, but Lu Ming hadn’t taken them. Who knew if they’d been used before? His focus was no longer on women.
Calming himself down, Lu Ming lay on the bed and began his exploration.
On the panel, the palace was a map.
He could spend time exploring, each session lasting fifteen minutes, with each exploration representing three percent progress.
Understanding the map clearly would also benefit him.
This was the right choice; after all, it was the palace, and countless eyes were watching him.

Lu Ming’s obedience, ironically, saved his life. A troop of battle-hardened soldiers patrolled outside constantly. Although the Imperial Guards had declined, their foundation remained strong; a real fight wouldn’t be easy.
The names of various locations appeared, along with the route: Daming Hall, Yangxin Hall, North Garden, the Inner Palace, Shufang Hall, Mingxin Hall, Yongxiang, and the Cold Palace.
The sky was already turning white, and the sun was rising. Lu Ming, deciding it was about time, got up and left.
Zhang Rang, having somehow received word of the situation, was also prepared early in the morning. After a long wait, Lu Ming got up. "Anmin, did you sleep well last night?"

"Thanks to Lord Zhang’s hospitality, I slept soundly. It’s getting late, and the day’s work begins in the morning. I plan to go see Lord Zhang’s son first, and then make further plans." Lu Ming knew what the other man was thinking. "Zhang Rang, I’m entrusting Wu Ban’s matter to you."

"Of course, of course. Anmin, please go ahead. This is my family’s token. Wherever you go, show this token, and my adopted son will know." Zhang Rang had naturally come for his adopted son. Lu Ming wasn’t worth his flattery, but Lu Ming’s medical skills were.
All of this was for his adopted son, for his descendants.
The pain of a parent outliving their child is unbearable. If he could be cured, all the better; if not, he would have to accept it.
With Zhang Rang seeing him off, the palace guards dared not cause trouble.
Instead, they remembered Lu Ming’s appearance, determined not to offend such a powerful figure in the future.
In the palace, the most important thing is to recognize faces, know who holds what position, and avoid offending or making things difficult for anyone.
Leaving the palace, Lu Ming finally saw Jiang Qin, who had been waiting outside all night. "Gongyi, go back to your residence and rest. I have some matters to attend to."

"Heh, my lord underestimates me. Back when we were fleeing—well, during the hunt—we didn’t sleep for three days and three nights. This is nothing. I’m well-rested." Jiang Qin laughed heartily. Since he had decided to pledge his loyalty, he would do his best.
Moreover, for his lord to allow him to stay overnight in the palace was a tremendous honor!
"Haha, good, then follow me." Lu Ming didn’t stand on ceremony, and with his entourage and personal guards, he headed east of the city. He mounted his horse and rode towards Zhang Feng’s residence.

The residence Zhang Rang chose for his adopted son was located in the east of the city. Its sheer size was astonishing. The main gate had three rooms, and the main hall, wing buildings, and rear building were arranged arbitrarily on both the east and west sides, typically with five to seven courtyards on each side. Gardens were attached to the back or sides of the residence, and some even included stables and family temples.
Compared to theirs, his own residence was truly quite simple.
The gatekeepers were initially reluctant to open the door, but upon hearing that Lu Ming had been sent by Zhang Rang, they dared not be negligent.

Normally, if someone came to curry favor or seek connections, they wouldn’t dare say such a thing. If it were discovered they weren’t, it wouldn’t be a simple matter of being driven away; they could be imprisoned!
Seeing the token in Lu Ming’s hand, the servants led him to the living room.

After a short while, a graceful young woman with a mature and alluring figure entered. Her phoenix eyes scanned the area, quickly settling on Lu Ming. "Does Your Excellency possess a token from Attendant Zhang?"
"The token is here." Lu Ming displayed the jade pendant.
The elegant young woman took the pendant and examined it carefully for a while before nodding and saying, "It is indeed Attendant Zhang’s token. May I ask your name, sir?"

Looking at the young woman before him, so poised and graceful, possessing the air of a well-bred lady, Lu Ming felt a touch of admiration. "My name is Lu Ming, Commandant of the Western Garden Army and concurrently Prefect of Longxi Commandery. Attendant Zhang entrusted me to examine his adopted son. May I ask who you are, madam?"

chapters.title: Chapter 111 Empress He’s sister
paragraphs: "I am He Shi, wife of Zhang Feng. The Empress in the palace is my elder sister. Since you, sir, were recommended by Zhang Changshi, I naturally trust you." The young woman introduced herself gracefully, subtly revealing her identity while also hinting at her status.
So she was Empress He’s younger sister, though historically, she was only mentioned briefly.
Empress He’s younger sister, her full sister.
General He Jin was Empress He’s half-brother, and General He Miao was her half-brother, originally named Zhu Miao, who changed his surname to He after his mother remarried He Zhen.

Lu Ming’s eyes flickered a few times as he looked at the graceful and beautiful young woman before him. If the younger sister was so beautiful and voluptuous, what kind of allure would the pampered Empress He possess?
"Madam Zhang, let’s begin the examination now."
"Yes, sir, please follow me." Madam He led the way, completely unsuspecting of Lu Ming; suspicion was futile.
He was introduced by Zhang Rang, and even if she didn’t like him, she had to put on a show and let him see him.
As the daughter-in-law of a eunuch, Madam He was somewhat resistant, but she had no choice but to accept her fate.
Fortunately, her husband wasn’t handsome, but he wasn’t arrogant or domineering, and treated her fairly well.
This was a typical arranged marriage, with each faction vying for power.
It wasn’t a simple division; it was a complex web of kinship, where everyone was intertwined.
The He family married their daughter to Zhang Rang’s adopted son to ease tensions, perhaps even at Emperor Ling’s behest.
After all, the emperor wanted to reclaim his power, and the establishment of the Eastern Han Dynasty was aided by powerful families.
Therefore, they could only use eunuchs and imperial relatives to counter the powerful families and regain some control.
The idea was good, and the execution was excellent.
However, sometimes things don’t go as planned.

For example, Emperor Ling intended to use his maternal relatives to counterbalance the powerful clans, but unexpectedly, this led to the Grand General being won over, effectively crippling this crucial right-hand man.
Lu Ming vaguely sensed this change—the change in the court, the change in the situation in Luoyang.
But all of this was irrelevant to him, and he couldn’t influence it. He only needed to seize the opportunity, fish in the chaos, and get what he wanted.
When he returned to Longxi Commandery, he might even be able to further expand his territory.
He could accumulate grain, delay declaring himself king, and once he captured Chang’an, occupied Guanzhong, and secured Tongguan, he could emulate Liu Bang.
He could watch the warlords of Guandong fight amongst themselves while he focused on his own development.
The land around Chang’an was fertile; he could develop it independently.
There are salt wells here that can be developed, allowing for trade with the Western Regions—a very favorable geographical location.
"Gongyi, you and your men wait here."
"Yes, my lord."
After passing through gardens, passageways, and then a garden with a pond, the vast mansion was built almost to the standards of royalty and nobility.
Zhang Rang’s adopted son was merely a commoner. Even with Zhang Rang’s immense power, he couldn’t arrange for his adopted son to enter officialdom; the path was fundamentally blocked.
It’s unimaginable what would happen if Zhang Rang were killed one day. Would Zhang Feng still be able to live here?
He would definitely be purged!

This is obvious even to a fool. The idea that "misfortune shouldn’t extend to family members" is utter nonsense. When it comes to purging, they’d dig up even ancestral graves; there’s no such thing as "misfortune shouldn’t extend to family members."
To truly "exclude family members from punishment," one needs sufficient power and strength; otherwise, it’s all empty talk and nonsense.
Lu Ming had been staring at Madam He’s shapely buttocks the entire way. Even hidden beneath her long, fringed dress, the roundness and firmness of her two peach-like buttocks were still visible.
She was truly a charming young woman. If he wasn’t mistaken, she must have given birth to possess such allure.
Madam He was unaware that she had been secretly watched. Her buttocks were indeed exquisite; even her sister, Empress He’s, peach-shaped buttocks were exceptional!
Plump yet not fat, firm yet not thin, a thrust from behind would produce waves of flesh and an astonishingly soft feedback—enough to make any man ejaculate wildly!
After winding through several turns, they finally arrived at a side room.
Even through the doorway, a strong smell of Chinese medicine wafted through the air; those who disliked it certainly wouldn’t.
Madam He covered her nose with barely concealed disgust. "My lord, my husband is inside."

"Very well, Madam, please sit quietly in the room." Lu Ming entered the room, which had been pushed open by a maid. He saw a thin man lying on a bed piled high with bedding, coughing occasionally. There were several jars on the floor; these weren’t medicine, but rather containers for his spitting.
The sickroom was utterly repulsive; no normal person would like it.
"Husband, this is the doctor my father found for you. Please let him examine you," Madam He said, forcing a smile, her eyes filled with disgust.
They already disliked each other, and with prolonged illness, even filial piety fades; the couple had become even less affectionate.
Lu Ming could tell at a glance that the man had tuberculosis, and in its late stages.
A cure would be extremely difficult; for now, they could only try to slow the progression of his illness.
"This is tuberculosis, and it’s tuberculosis that has accumulated over time."

He knew this even before taking Zhang Feng’s pulse. Lu Ming took a stool and sat down, pretending to take Zhang Feng’s pulse. "It’s fortunate you’ve encountered me; it might not be the same with others. Now that you’ve been ill for a long time, treatment will be a long process. I’ll give you acupuncture first, after which you might vomit, to expel the pus and pus from your sores. Then, with medication, you’ll gradually get better."
"Cough cough, doctor, is there any hope for me?" Zhang Feng’s breathing was very weak, as if he might die at any moment.

"Yes." Lu Ming finished speaking and said to Madam He, "Madam, have the servants cook a pot of plain porridge. The vegetables only need to be steamed. Three days later, the meat needs to be chopped into small pieces and mixed into the porridge. Continue this for a month, and you’ll be able to get out of bed and walk."
Without giving him a chance to refuse, Lu Ming began to perform acupuncture.
The calcined silver needles were inserted into Zhang Feng’s body with lightning speed, a sight to behold.
In reality, however, this was merely Lu Ming’s skill casting process; once the casting was complete, the treatment would be finished.
Throughout the process, he felt as if he were being controlled, inserting needles into suitable acupoints to stimulate them.
No need for any knowledge of acupuncture; the system would handle everything for him.
