chapters.title: Chapter 112 Seducing a married woman surnamed He
paragraphs: Half an hour later, Zhang Feng was able to drink plain porridge, something unthinkable before. He used to cough incessantly, unable to eat anything. He would vomit after eating, a very troublesome situation.
Looking at her husband’s gradual improvement, Madam He’s eyes showed no joy, only calm. "Thank you so much, sir! Your miraculous healing is truly my greatest gratitude!"

"Madam, you’re too kind. I see you also have some hidden ailments, some years old, likely from the past. Illness comes like a landslide, but recovery is slow and gradual. Would you like me to take a look?" Lu Ming handed the prescription to Madam He after writing it down, and said this almost impulsively.
He figured he could use the pretext of treating her illness to get closer, perhaps even seducing this charming young woman!
After all, Zhang Feng was a patient and incapable of sexual relations.
Besides, the medication needed to treat tuberculosis was still under research, a process that involved many layers of research.
Moreover, some require raw materials and processing; the entire process necessitates unlocking at least dozens of blueprints, each intricately linked, making it impossible to operate independently.
Madam He was startled. She took the prescription, glanced at it for a moment, and then handed it to a maid, instructing her to fetch the medicine. "Why do you say this, sir?"

"Madam, do you experience periods of severe lower abdominal pain every month? Do you often feel dizzy and weak? These are the initial signs of illness; your body is reminding you that it needs treatment. Just like when you’re hungry, your stomach growls; when you’re thirsty, your throat dries out—these are all warnings." Lu Ming spoke of common problems in life, yet it seemed somewhat unsettling, as if there was a hidden truth.
Like an apple falling—everyone knows it’s ripe, but no one thinks about why.
"Indeed, then I’ll trouble you to examine me, sir." Madam He didn’t refuse; instead, she wanted to see if it would be effective.
The two went to a side room, where Lu Ming examined Madam He in a proper and conventional manner.

"Madam, when you experience abdominal pain again, you can gently massage it with your hands to reduce the pain. Acupuncture can also alleviate the pain. Drinking a decoction of ginger and brown sugar can also relieve the pain and discomfort. Pay attention to your diet; avoid bland food and rich, fatty foods," Lu Ming explained while taking her pulse. He then examined her face. "Madam, could you please stick out your tongue so I can see if there are any other symptoms?"

This was a very impolite act; sticking out one’s tongue in front of others, especially a woman, was considered very inappropriate. However, seeing Lu Ming’s skillful medical technique, Madam He still suppressed her shame and stuck out her tongue.

"Hmm, she has some internal heat, and Madam’s stomach isn’t very good either; she needs some conditioning. Acupuncture would be better, but it might be inconvenient. Prescriptions will alleviate the symptoms, though the effect will be minimal, better than nothing." Lu Ming spoke to himself, then looked up at Madam He, a hint of self-deprecation in his voice, "I apologize, Madam, I’ve always been like this. Fortunately, His Majesty didn’t blame me when I treated him."
"Oh? You’ve even treated His Majesty?" Madam He was somewhat intrigued. She remembered her mother’s poor health; perhaps Lu Ming could help.
However, she’d have to wait and see.

"I have. I’ve seen Yang Cong, the Prefect of Chang’an, Marquis Zhao, and His Majesty. I’ve also treated the Grand Commandant and his wife." Lu Ming recounted his glorious deeds with great familiarity.
"If it weren’t for the separation of men and women, I could treat the most difficult and complicated illnesses. I am proficient in acupuncture, which is why it’s inconvenient when treating women."

chapters.title: Chapter 116 Sign a death contract
paragraphs: Upon entering, Lu Ming immediately felt all eyes on him.
If he hadn’t possessed exceptional self-control, he would likely be drenched in sweat.
Among the assembled ministers, some were so powerful that a mere stomp of their feet could shake the entire city of Luoyang.
Others were representatives of powerful families or members of their clans. Seeing Lu Ming again, they took this suddenly appearing commoner in the court seriously, perhaps considering him useful.
This use wasn’t necessarily for personal gain; it might even be the kind of use where someone’s head is used for a purpose.
"Your subject greets Your Majesty," Lu Ming said, ignoring the stares of the others, and bowed to Emperor Ling.

"Rise," Emperor Ling said impatiently, his obese body seated on the dragon throne. "Lu Ming, General Huwei says his son was seduced. You were bullying the weak with a gun, injuring someone, and killing someone in the street. What do you have to say?"
Lu Ming found it somewhat amusing to see the middle-aged general, who had been so animated just moments before, now glaring at him angrily.
First the young one, now the old one.
Is this never going to end?

"Like father, like son! If the father is a coward, the son will surely be a good-for-nothing. I think General Tiger Might is just using his position to intimidate others; he has absolutely no ability and only knows how to point fingers. When it comes to a real battle, he’ll probably be the first to abandon his soldiers and army and flee. Such a person is utterly disgusting!"

"You! What nonsense are you spouting! You’re making baseless accusations! Your mouth is full of filth! You bastard, born of a mother but without a father to teach you!" Wu Kuang retorted angrily, immediately reopening old wounds, showing no trace of a general’s demeanor, but rather resembling a thug.

Lu Ming’s smile remained, but the murderous glint in his eyes was enough to kill. Instead of immediately attacking, he clasped his hands in a fist salute to Emperor Ling and said, "Your Majesty, General Wu Kuang is disrespectful to the Emperor, a traitor to his master and ancestors, and utterly disrespectful to Your Majesty. His own son is a bully who incites public resentment, and he claims to be the most powerful man in Luoyang—this is blatant disrespect! Your Majesty, Wu Kuang insulted my late father, who sacrificed his life fighting against foreign invaders who plundered our Han dynasty. Such slander and defamation cannot be tolerated. I request to sign a life-or-death contract with Wu Kuang, a duel in the ring, where fate will decide!"
This was a legal way to kill him!

Moreover, a life-or-death contract, as the name suggests, is a contract for a battle until one side is defeated. Whether one is killed is entirely up to luck, and even if someone is killed, there is no responsibility!

"Wu Kuang, you old dog, if you don’t dare to fight, then don’t wear armor anymore. Just put on some rouge, change into women’s clothes, and become a woman!" Lu Ming sneered mockingly, wishing he could kill this old dog on the spot.
Without further ado, let’s get straight to the fight.

"Oh? A life-or-death contract? Anmin, that’s a new thing." Emperor Ling was intrigued. He wasn’t interested in how the fight went, but he was very interested in hand-to-hand combat and the visceral, bloody clashes.

"Your Majesty," Lu Ming said, "the life-or-death agreement is a written contract, ensuring both sides will fight without hesitation and with all their might. Since we are all leaders of troops, let’s test our mettle with swords, spears, and fists. The winner takes the loser’s fortune, and the loser loses everything. Furthermore, I suggest we have a betting operation, involving all the officials, the nobles, and wealthy merchants of Luoyang, to see who the real coward is!" Lu Ming’s sudden idea of a betting operation was essentially a gambling den.
He didn’t explicitly name Emperor Ling to participate, only hinting at it, but there was definitely significant profit involved!
Sure enough, Emperor Ling’s eyes lit up, as if he had seen a brand new money-making opportunity.
Since these former generals were no longer reliable, could he use this method to purge them?
Did it matter who was right and who was wrong?
What mattered was that everyone was convinced, and he didn’t need to show too much favoritism or go too far.
"A bet seems a bit excessive, but it’s also a very good, very good idea!"
Yuan Kui immediately understood Emperor Ling’s intentions upon seeing his expression.
This emperor was incompetent and absurd, but he was the emperor, and some things couldn’t be stopped.
Moreover, the more absurd the emperor was, the more beneficial it was to the powerful clans.

At least, since the emperor only thought about making money, it was difficult to restrict him further. This was a tacit understanding built up over twenty years: power couldn’t be compromised for money!
"Your Majesty, judging right and wrong based on a bet is unfair."

"Your Majesty, I believe it’s feasible." Grand Commandant Zhang Wen stepped forward, having seen his brother-in-law, Marquis Zhao, nod in approval. To maintain his position, he needed to be close to his brother-in-law.
"I object."
"I object."
As soon as Yuan Kui spoke, the officials below joined in the opposition.
The Yuan family’s influence was no joke.
Offending the emperor might mean death, or it might go unpunished, but offending the Yuan family would certainly mean a fate worse than death—don’t doubt that.
Emperor Ling, however, remained unconvinced. He had always been very interested in matters of money.

"Very well, it’s decided then. Since the Grand Commandant agrees, there must be a reason for this. Very good, Grand Commandant, the arena wager is yours to handle. Lu Ming, Wu Kuang, you two sign a death pact. Three days later, in front of the South Palace Gate, you will publicly settle your score. The loser will bear all responsibility, and the winner will inherit the loser’s estate. That’s it, court adjourned!"
No one expected such an outcome. It was utterly outrageous! Absurd beyond belief, utterly absurd!
But what could be done?
This kind of ridiculous thing had happened more than once or twice. When has it ever been successfully stopped?

As long as the emperor didn’t interfere with the Ministry of Personnel, and didn’t concern himself with disaster relief or the long-standing drought... Neither the Yuan nor the Yang families would interfere; they still held the reins of power!
Faced with Lu Ming’s murderous intent and witnessing his throat-slitting gesture, Wu Kuang was filled with lingering fear and dread.
He was terrified by Lu Ming’s previous display of fighting prowess, and terrified that Emperor Ling had actually agreed to such an absurd life-or-death duel!

"What are you afraid of, Wu Kuang? You are General Tiger Might, and that’s just a greenhorn. What are you afraid of? Look at him, his beard isn’t even fully grown yet. Hmph, a young whippersnapper is unreliable. We’ll kill him when the time comes!" General He Jin frowned slightly. Things had taken an unexpected turn. He needed to go back and sort things out to see what had happened!

"The emperor wants to punish you, and you have to accept it. That’s the emperor’s nature; the emperor is never wrong!"
Moreover, this gamble could yield a large sum of money, which was the key point. With money, you can get everything.
His own medical treatment cost money, building a new army cost money, maintaining the palace cost money—even the emperor was short of money!
After court, news spread quickly that Lu Ming and Wu Kuang had a life-or-death duel, and that Zhang Rang had personally led men to set up a stall!
No one expected it to turn out this way. This behavior was so absurd, so ridiculous, yet so perfectly reasonable.
Was Emperor Ling absurd?
Absurd!
Extremely absurd, even utterly lacking the qualities of a wise ruler!
But so what?
He was the emperor, the Son of Heaven—that was enough!

The imperial court openly announced that positions ranging from Marquis of Guannei down to the Tiger Guards and Feathered Forest Guards under the Grand Master of Ceremonies could be purchased with money.

The regulations for selling official positions were: local officials cost twice as much as central officials, while county officials had varying prices; promotions also required payment based on the price.
Those seeking official positions could bid, and the highest bidder would be appointed.
In addition to fixed prices, the prices were subject to change based on the applicant’s social standing and wealth.

Generally, the price of an official position was calculated based on the official’s annual salary. For example, a position with an annual salary of 2,000 shi (a unit of grain measure) cost 20 million coins, and a position with an annual salary of 400 shi cost 4 million coins—meaning the price of an official position was 10,000 times the official’s annual income.
Many officials were deterred by the exorbitant "official fee" and resigned.
This was outrageous, utterly outrageous.
This is why, even with layers of deception, Emperor Ling still amassed a vast amount of money.

The powerful clans, gritting their teeth, tolerated this, and instead used the opportunity to control key departments, intensifying their exploitation, which ultimately led to the Yellow Turban Rebellion.
On one occasion, Emperor Ling showed a surprising interest in donkeys. Whether he had never seen them before or had some new pastime was unclear.
A eunuch who frequently served Emperor Ling, noticing his displeasure, carefully selected four donkeys and led them to him.

Upon seeing the four donkeys, Emperor Ling’s eyes lit up with excitement. He immediately ordered someone skilled in driving a donkey cart to be found, and he himself rode in the cart, embarking on a day trip around the palace.
Unexpectedly, after a few days, Emperor Ling grew tired of the ride and suddenly decided to drive the donkey cart himself, touring the palace every day, thoroughly enjoying himself.
Within days, news of the emperor riding in a donkey cart spread far and wide beyond the palace.
The high-ranking officials and nobles in the capital thought to themselves,
"Hey, is even the emperor that trendy? I can’t fall behind!"
Since their own emperor was so trendy, no one wanted to be left behind, and they all started imitating him, causing a surge in donkey prices for a while.
But Emperor Ling’s enthusiasm was short-lived. Just as riding in a donkey cart became fashionable, he got bored.
Such absurd things happened one after another, so when Emperor Ling once again held a martial arts contest to determine who was right and who was wrong, the people of Luoyang were already used to it.

On the contrary, they were extremely curious about a certain gambling den that had opened. The odds listed were for two people: Lu Ming’s odds were 1 to 1, and Wu Kuang’s were 2 to 1. It didn’t seem special, and it seemed that Wu Kuang was the better one.
Furthermore, rumors had already spread that Lu Ming’s strength was negligible, while Wu Kuang possessed immense strength, capable of tearing apart a tiger alive!
This was all a publicity stunt, designed to entice bettors to place their bets on Wu Kuang, thus allowing the emperor to make a fortune.
As for why he wasn’t afraid of Lu Ming being killed, it seemed Emperor Ling had other plans. Keeping Lu Ming by his side for daily recuperation, serving as a private physician, wouldn’t be bad.
This was only because Lu Ming held an official position and had achieved some merit; otherwise, his medical skills might have turned him into a private slave.
In Luoyang, any wrong step could lead to utter ruin.
Who could have imagined that Emperor Ling, who had always valued Lu Ming, would have such a plan?
Even Marquis Zhao had some reservations about Lu Ming because of his eldest son’s affair. A dog is a dog; nothing can change its nature.
While the rumors swirled outside, Lu Ming was at the Grand Commandant’s residence, embracing the Grand Commandant’s wife, Liu Liu, on their bed, speaking these words.
Madam Zhang was dressed in tattered clothes, and their genitals were still intimately connected, clearly indicating that they had engaged in sexual activity.
Moreover, the semen had begun to liquefy and leak out over time.
"A duel to determine the victor? Hmph, I think His Majesty has ulterior motives. This won’t be good for you." Liu Liu leaned against Lu Ming’s chest, her restless desires calming considerably.
A woman in middle age, whose desires have been satisfied, even has skin that appears more radiant.
"Has my brother made any statement?"
"No, probably because he’s taking his anger out on Liu Zan." Lu Ming shook his head, narrowing his eyes as he considered the possibilities.
He had long known that Luoyang wouldn’t be peaceful. Even if he kept a low profile, someone would deliberately cause trouble.
The Yuan family would definitely not let him get away so easily; they would love for him to lose the battle so they could find a reason to execute him.

"None of my brother’s sons are any good. Liu Zan is a complete waste. My brother sent him to study in Jingzhou, but he was sent back in disgrace after less than six months. What a useless piece of trash." Liu Liu bluntly pointed out her nephew’s shortcomings and dark history. She was, after all, his aunt, yet she had abandoned him because of her lover.
"It’s alright, I’m used to it. Only by reaching a certain position can one be taken seriously. Don’t worry, I’m fine." Lu Ming didn’t seem to care much; he didn’t react to such things.

Liu Liu suddenly perked up, her eyes sparkling. "Wu Kuang’s family is quite wealthy, and their mansion is in the south, much larger than where you live now. If you defeat him, you can take over his mansion and shops."

"Heh, fine. Let him be my stepping stone!" Lu Ming knew that in this conflict, he had only gained a small share, not the lion’s share. The Emperor ate the meat, others drank the soup, and he was lucky to get a little bit of the broth. Public opinion has little influence, and the benefits are directly proportional to one’s abilities; there’s nothing that can be done about it.

chapters.title: Chapter 118 Yang’s Choice
paragraphs: It was already late when Lu Ming left the Grand Commandant’s residence.
He returned home and went to the courtyard. He took out the smelted ore and forged it into copper plates.
The sound of the hammer striking metal, coupled with his profuse sweating profusely—sweat streaming down his muscular physique—made even the maids blush.
He forged the copper plates into a spearhead, then pulled out extracted fibers and began weaving them into a thin rope.
Two fibers were combined into one rope, and two more ropes were woven together over fifteen minutes to form a sturdy rope.
With the rope, he attached it to the spearhead and used the system to create a climbing rope, allowing him to traverse obstacles like high walls.
Preparing for the competition three days later, Lu Ming didn’t underestimate his opponent despite their age; on the contrary, he prepared thoroughly.
That evening, he focused on crafting practical equipment for himself and even specially prepared some stones to smelt in the furnace.
The furnace was completed a few days ago, but it takes two days to reach a temperature high enough to smelt stones.
With bellows, it could be done even faster, reaching maximum temperature in half a day.
During the day, Lu Ming went out to recruit soldiers and horses, hiring some wandering knights.
He also promulgated the rules for the lower ranks, and the knights all hoped to be promoted to regular soldiers.
Eating royal food was far better than licking blood from the edge of a knife.
Moreover, one of Lu Ming’s rules was that military pay would not be withheld; what was due would be paid in full and on time.
Although it sounded so appealing, most people still had doubts.
Because receiving pay without working was commonplace; it was just a matter of whether it was investigated, and if investigated, it was always discovered.
Soldiers were poor; no one would join the army unless forced by circumstances.
In the Eastern Han Dynasty, joining the army meant death. If the soldier died, and he was the breadwinner of his family, then that family would collapse!
Therefore, enlisting was out of the question unless absolutely necessary.
Sounding it good was useless; as a result, very few people volunteered. Recruiting in Luoyang was practically impossible; they would have to look to the surrounding areas.
The Yuan Family.

Yuan Kui patiently listened to his servant’s report, then knelt on the seat of honor. After taking a sip of tea, he sneered, "Recruiting in Luoyang? Hmph, a pipe dream! You can’t even gather enough men; let’s see what you’re capable of!"

Want to get supplies from the Grand Minister of Agriculture? First, they’d have to gather the men. Right now, Marquis Zhao had to advance the funds before Lu Ming had the qualifications and resources to recruit soldiers.

"Uncle, the day after tomorrow is the life-or-death duel between Lu Ming and Wu Kuang. If Wu Kuang wins, will the General still be loyal to us?" Yuan Shao asked, voicing his doubts. He was willing to cheer, but truly severing all ties was difficult for him.

He could dominate Hebei, control Youzhou, Jizhou, Qingzhou, and Bingzhou, and command hundreds of thousands of troops, yet he still suffered a crushing defeat at Guandu. It can only be said that his talent stopped there.
He had countless choices, but he chose the worst one, which, in a way, is quite bizarre.

"It’s alright, He Jin alone can’t turn the tide. His Majesty is currently dissatisfied with him. If Wu Kuang wins, we’ll win him over. If Wu Kuang loses, He Jin will be even more loyal to us." Yuan Wei was confident of this; the Yuan family held the reins of the court.
Sometimes, those in high positions inevitably engage in social maneuvering, securing positions for relatives or doing other favors.
This requires an exchange of interests. Once or twice, it will happen three or four times, and over time, a bond of interest is formed, making it difficult to step down.
On the contrary, the Yuan family can actively abandon them, thus gaining absolute initiative.

He Jin is a Grand General, but how long can he hold out? Emperor Ling’s health wasn’t good. He’d have less than ten years left at most, and ten years was enough time for the Yuan family to plan their next move.
Yuan Shao also held He Jin in low esteem, considering him nothing more than a butcher.
In fact, He Jin lacked decisiveness, which explained Yuan Shao’s disdain.
"I see, I understand! I’ve learned something!"

Yuan Kui nodded with satisfaction, then, as if remembering something, said, "If you accompany the army this time, you can go to Ye City to bolster your reputation and pave a good omen for your future appointment in Bohai."

The future plans for the Yuan family members were already predetermined: go out to take up positions, cultivate loyal followers, consolidate power, then return to their posts, relying on nepotism to monopolize promotions.
Not only Yuan Shao, but even Yuan Shu had already been arranged—to become a prefect in Yingchuan, to cultivate relationships with the local faction, where there were many Yuan family protégés.
"But showing off a bit will prevent them from forgetting who the real master is!"
"Yes, Uncle," Yuan Shao bowed respectfully. He wasn’t too worried about his future, but competing for the heirship was proving difficult.

A powerful family only has the resources to propel someone to a high position; it’s either him or Yuan Shu. As for Yuan Ji, he was destined to be just a brick in the city gate, never reaching great heights.
Keeping him in one place ensures the Yuan family’s minimum standing.

Not only the Yuan family, but even the Yang family was paying attention to this matter. Lu Ming was introduced to Zhao Hou by their Yang family, and now he was a favorite of Emperor Ling; they could try to win him over to some extent.
Two days later, at the Yang family’s residence.
Yang Biao sat in his seat, listening to his cousin Yang Cong’s report. His brow furrowed, deep in thought. "You mean he came to treat you again today?"

"Yes, I asked him about tomorrow’s plans. He didn’t seem particularly worried, not exactly enthusiastic, but unusually calm. Brother, do you think this could be His Majesty’s scheme? To lure the snake out of its hole?" Yang Cong had just received acupuncture today to treat his syphilis, so he needed Lu Ming to live as long as possible.

Narrowing his eyes, Yang Biao remembered his father’s words and instructed, "Here’s what you’ll do: go to his residence and invite him to a gathering tomorrow, and also to have the old ancestor examine him. If he wins, then let him marry Xiao Shiwu."
Xiao Shiwu was actually Yang Biao’s daughter, a child born late in life, whom he doted on.
However, in a large family, no matter how much love is shown, daughters are ultimately used for political marriages.
Coincidentally, his daughter was also of marriageable age.
The Yang family’s style wouldn’t consider someone too high or too low; someone suitable would suffice.
Therefore, even if Lu Ming came from a humble background, Yang Biao, as the head of the family, could still arrange for his daughter to marry him off.
Status was insignificant; as long as he became Yang’s son-in-law, he would naturally have status, which was of no importance.
What Yang Biao valued were Lu Ming’s current medical skills, his position, and his standing in the eyes of the Spirit Emperor.

chapters.title: Chapter 121 In the blink of an eye
paragraphs: Early morning brought a flurry of activity to Luoyang.
Peddlers and laborers went about their daily lives, everyone bustling about to make a living.
But today, many spoiled young masters woke up exceptionally early.
This unusually early rise wasn’t for studying or practicing martial arts, but rather to catch a theatrical performance!
Today was the duel between Lu Ming, the Western Garden Army Commandant, and Wu Kuang, the Tiger General!
The cause was that Wu Kuang’s son, Wu Ban, had assaulted Feng Fang’s daughter, only to be stopped by Lu Ming, who intervened and drove the boy away.
It was said that even the arm of Wang Yue’s nephew, the greatest swordsman in the land, had been shattered. With such a terrifying feat, the outcome was anyone’s guess!
If it were just about watching a play, it might not have captured everyone’s attention.
But within three days, almost everyone in Luoyang knew about it, and that the Grand Commandant was placing bets on behalf of the Emperor, gambling on who would win!
The emperor using the lives of his ministers as stakes for his amusement is utterly absurd!
Yet everyone flocks to it, and Wu Kuang has spread the word that he will surely take Lu Ming’s life on the arena!
This leads many to bet on Wu Kuang, after all, he is a high-ranking official under the Grand General, possessing both ability and fighting prowess.
Court intrigues are none of the common people’s business, nor do they want to.
But today is different; everyone can place bets, anyone with spare cash can bet.
Emperor Ling’s reputation may be absurd, but he disdains deceiving people.
Therefore, many wealthy people have placed bets, and even some commoners with spare cash have placed bets.
And the imperial ministers, the highest officials, all have to place bets to determine who is right and who is wrong.
In reality, this is completely unnecessary, because their opinions on right and wrong are meaningless.
Whoever wins is right.
So what’s the point of betting?
It’s simply throwing money into Emperor Ling’s pocket!
He could have just robbed it directly, but now he’s using a different method to demand it. Emperor Ling is really giving him too much face!
Lu Ming has already bet three thousand taels on himself; that’s his limit.
Many things require money. In Luoyang, even buying materials costs money.
Moreover, maintaining the mansion is a considerable expense.
But if he acquires Wu Kuang’s assets and gets some shops, he could try to cover his living expenses.
In the morning, he once again climaxed on the alluring Yi Jin, and then had a long French kiss with the young Wang Li.
Lu Ming finally got up; today was the same as always.
Having defeated Wu Kuang, and with the olive branch from the Yang family, his days ahead will be a little better.
But it’s limited, because the Yang family is also a powerful clan, and they won’t be kind to him for no reason.
If he gets too close, he will inevitably be targeted by Emperor Ling. Currently unable to become a chess player, one can only keep a low profile.
North Gate Training Ground.
The captain on duty today felt more sweaty than ever before, simply because there were too many people here.

Moreover, Emperor Ling would be present to observe, and the Three Dukes and Nine Ministers would also be there. These people, who could crush him with a flick of their toes in normal times, were now all gathered together. If anything went wrong, his head would truly roll!

"Go tell the captain to send reinforcements. His Majesty’s safety is paramount." The squad leader wiped away his sweat. He was overwhelmed, and he also had to assign men to prevent commoners from entering the palace—a matter of utmost importance.
Before the training ground, a platform five meters high and ten meters long had been erected. This was for the duels; there was nothing else there, just the platform.

Emperor Ling arrived at the city tower early, and looking at the surging crowd below, he felt a surge of pride. He was the ruler of all under heaven; he was the Son of Heaven, the Emperor, and his word was law.
"His Majesty has arrived! Kneel and pay your respects!" Zhang Rang shrieked, and the eunuch in front of him echoed his cry.
Instantly, all the commoners knelt, paying their respects to the Liu Emperor.
"Greetings, Your Majesty!"
"Hmm, rise!" Emperor Ling enjoyed the feeling of being worshipped by thousands. "Today is the duel to the death between the Lower Army Colonel and General Tiger Might. Let them begin."
Emperor Ling’s arrival brought a quiet to the scene. The distance between them was nearly three miles, so there was no need to worry about a surprise attack.
A eunuch stepped onto the platform and shouted, "Please welcome Lower Army Colonel Lu Ming to the stage!"
Lu Ming, carrying a long spear, walked step by step up the steps. Commoners around him were also chanting his name, cheering him on.
He knew this was not out of concern for him, but rather because they had bet on his victory.
His steps were steady, his eyes fixed ahead.
Today’s battle was one of victory or defeat!
Emperor Ling whispered to Zhang Rang, "Is everything ready?"
"Ready, Your Majesty, do not worry," Zhang Rang replied, indicating his readiness. In reality, Emperor Ling didn’t want Lu Ming to die.
At this crucial moment, he needed to protect Lu Ming, making him obediently serve as his personal physician.
Of course, this was in the guise of a eunuch; whether Lu Ming was willing or not was beyond his control!
If Lu Ming won, this tactic wouldn’t be necessary.
Once Lu Ming stood on the platform, the eunuch shouted in a hoarse voice, "Please welcome General Wu Kuang, the Tiger General, to the platform!"
Compared to Lu Ming, who wasn’t even wearing armor, Wu Kuang was clad in heavy, gleaming armor, with a breastplate, and held a long spear in both hands.
He immediately assumed an offensive stance, spear pointed at Lu Ming. If it weren’t for the opportune moment, he would have attacked immediately.
"You two can begin preparing. Three, two, one, the match begins!" The eunuch had barely finished shouting when Wu Kuang darted forward, spear aimed straight for Lu Ming’s head.

Facing the straight-forward spear, Lu Ming merely deflected it a few times. When the spear tip was less than centimeters from him, he suddenly flicked the end of the spear shaft with his right hand, the rebound force deflecting Wu Kuang’s spear tip.
This action caught Wu Kuang off guard, sending him flying. Lu Ming then drew a dagger from behind his back, swiftly stepped forward, and decapitated Wu Kuang!
*Thud!* Wu Kuang’s head flew high into the air, his body remaining stationary. A column of blood shot into the sky. In the blink of an eye, the battle was decided!
"Utterly worthless trash." Lu Ming wiped the dagger on Wu Kuang’s body before putting it away, a gesture brimming with arrogance and disdain!

Emperor Ling is really giving him too much face!
Lu Ming has already bet three thousand taels on himself; that’s his limit.
Many things require money.
In Luoyang, even buying materials costs money.
Moreover, maintaining the mansion is a considerable expense.
But if he acquires Wu Kuang’s assets and gets some shops, he could try to cover his living expenses.
In the morning, he once again climaxed on the alluring Yi Jin, and then had a long French kiss with the young Wang Li.
Lu Ming finally got up; today was the same as always.
Having defeated Wu Kuang, and with the olive branch from the Yang family, his days ahead will be a little better.
But it’s limited, because the Yang family is also a powerful clan, and they won’t be kind to him for no reason.
If he gets too close, he will inevitably be targeted by Emperor Ling.
Currently unable to become a chess player, one can only keep a low profile.
North Gate Training Ground.
The captain on duty today felt more sweaty than ever before, simply because there were too many people here.
Moreover, Emperor Ling would be present to observe, and the Three Dukes and Nine Ministers would also be there.
These people, who could crush him with a flick of their toes in normal times, were now all gathered together.
If anything went wrong, his head would truly roll!
"Go tell the captain to send reinforcements.
His Majesty’s safety is paramount." The squad leader wiped away his sweat.
He was overwhelmed, and he also had to assign men to prevent commoners from entering the palace—a matter of utmost importance.
Before the training ground, a platform five meters high and ten meters long had been erected.
This was for the duels; there was nothing else there, just the platform.
Emperor Ling arrived at the city tower early, and looking at the surging crowd below, he felt a surge of pride.
He was the ruler of all under heaven; he was the Son of Heaven, the Emperor, and his word was law.
"His Majesty has arrived!
Kneel and pay your respects!" Zhang Rang shrieked, and the eunuch in front of him echoed his cry.
Instantly, all the commoners knelt, paying their respects to the Liu Emperor.
"Greetings, Your Majesty!"
"Hmm, rise!" Emperor Ling enjoyed the feeling of being worshipped by thousands.
"Today is the duel to the death between the Lower Army Colonel and General Tiger Might.
Let them begin."
Emperor Ling’s arrival brought a quiet to the scene.
The distance between them was nearly three miles, so there was no need to worry about a surprise attack.
A eunuch stepped onto the platform and shouted, "Please welcome Lower Army Colonel Lu Ming to the stage!"
Lu Ming, carrying a long spear, walked step by step up the steps.
Commoners around him were also chanting his name, cheering him on.
He knew this was not out of concern for him, but rather because they had bet on his victory.
His steps were steady, his eyes fixed ahead.
Today’s battle was one of victory or defeat!
Emperor Ling whispered to Zhang Rang, "Is everything ready?"
"Ready, Your Majesty, do not worry," Zhang Rang replied, indicating his readiness.
In reality, Emperor Ling didn’t want Lu Ming to die.
At this crucial moment, he needed to protect Lu Ming, making him obediently serve as his personal physician.
Of course, this was in the guise of a eunuch; whether Lu Ming was willing or not was beyond his control!
If Lu Ming won, this tactic wouldn’t be necessary.
Once Lu Ming stood on the platform, the eunuch shouted in a hoarse voice, "Please welcome General Wu Kuang, the Tiger General, to the platform!"
Compared to Lu Ming, who wasn’t even wearing armor, Wu Kuang was clad in heavy, gleaming armor, with a breastplate, and held a long spear in both hands.
He immediately assumed an offensive stance, spear pointed at Lu Ming.
If it weren’t for the opportune moment, he would have attacked immediately.
"You two can begin preparing.
Three, two, one, the match begins!" The eunuch had barely finished shouting when Wu Kuang darted forward, spear aimed straight for Lu Ming’s head.
Facing the straight-forward spear, Lu Ming merely deflected it a few times.
When the spear tip was less than centimeters from him, he suddenly flicked the end of the spear shaft with his right hand, the rebound force deflecting Wu Kuang’s spear tip.
This action caught Wu Kuang off guard, sending him flying.
Lu Ming then drew a dagger from behind his back, swiftly stepped forward, and decapitated Wu Kuang!
*Thud!* Wu Kuang’s head flew high into the air, his body remaining stationary.
A column of blood shot into the sky.
In the blink of an eye, the battle was decided!
"Utterly worthless trash." Lu Ming wiped the dagger on Wu Kuang’s body before putting it away, a gesture brimming with arrogance and disdain!

chapters.title: Chapter 122 The waiter is finished
paragraphs: "Father!" The moment Wu Ban saw his father fall, his eyes widened in rage, staring intently at Lu Ming as if he wanted to devour him.
Lu Ming turned and saw him, giving him a thumbs-up before abruptly turning it back in a defiant gesture.
Then he made a throat-slitting motion, pointing at Wu Kuang’s headless corpse, as if implying that Wu Ban would also be beheaded!
"Ah! You beast! Pay with your life! Pay for my father’s life!" Wu Ban roared, grabbing his sword and charging forward, unstoppable by those around him.
In the heat of youth, he couldn’t tolerate such provocation.
This behavior was utterly beastly; even he would die!
Killing someone’s father and then provoking them—this was outrageous, utterly outrageous! How could he be so cruel!
The moment Lu Ming saw the glint in Wu Ban’s eyes, he knew he had to eliminate this man.
A person who holds a grudge will stop at nothing to deal with him.
Therefore, he must be careful. He must eliminate the threat completely, leaving no chance for the other party.
He stepped forward, his spear thrusting out. A flash of cold light appeared first, then the shaft spun, increasing the spear’s destructive power.
Finally, it pierced straight into Wu Ban’s throat, the spear tip piercing through his spine.
He slammed the spear shaft down, the shockwave tearing Wu Ban’s head apart!
*Thud!* His entire head turned into a bloody mist, a gruesome sight, a one-hit kill, giving him no chance to resist!
"Ah! Murder!"
"Ah! Too, too terrifying!"
This cruelty made even the Spirit Emperor’s heart pound. He hadn’t expected the previously respectful Lu Ming to have such violent tendencies; it was truly terrifying!
After completing his task, Lu Ming bowed deeply to Emperor Ling, saying, "Thanks to Your Majesty’s grace, I have fulfilled my mission and slew the villain Wu Kuang."
"Good, good, very good. You did well, Lu Ming. Go back; you will receive what you deserve. Prepare the carriage and return to the palace." Emperor Ling suddenly remembered that he was the emperor!
No matter how strong or capable Lu Ming was, he was still just a subject. Could he possibly overturn the heavens?
Lu Ming maintained this posture until Emperor Ling had been gone for a long time before he rose.
His expression remained impeccably respectful.
Today he had won, which meant he was right.
Wu Kuang died because he was too weak!
The law of the jungle—this was clearly and vividly demonstrated!
Some people cursed, while others laughed loudly.

Grand Commandant Zhang Wen led an army, escorting boxes. Ten minor officials began checking account books, clearly starting to fulfill their promises. Those who had bet on Lu Ming could now exchange their money!
Attendant Fu Wan approached, smiling and bowing to Lu Ming, "My lord, it’s an honor to meet you. I am Fu Wan. I’m here to accompany you on the investigation of Wu Kuang’s property. Please!"
Fu Wan!
Upon hearing this name, Lu Ming couldn’t help but glance at the man a few more times. This old man, nearly fifty, was Fu Shou’s father!
Fu Wan wasn’t particularly famous. What made Lu Ming remember him was that Fu Wan’s daughter was named Fu Shou, the first empress of Emperor Xian of Han!
Having an empress as a daughter naturally attracted a lot of attention.
However, at this time, Fu Wan wasn’t famous; he was considered a member of the imperial family. His wife was Liu Hua, the daughter of Emperor Heng, making him the imperial son-in-law.
"Of course, of course, Lord Fu, please!" Lu Ming immediately put on a smiling expression. Since the other party had a daughter destined to be empress, then he wouldn’t be so lenient!

Originally, he had planned to stay in Luoyang for a while to develop his strength, but now it seemed he should focus his attention on these married women and young girls. Only with women could he experience the so-called ultimate pleasure!
In ancient times, confiscating property was a kind of pleasure. Lu Ming took his personal guards with him.
On the way, Fu Wan deliberately tried to get close to Lu Ming, and Lu Ming readily agreed, saying whatever came to mind.
Today’s battle had opened up the situation. He was no longer an unknown nobody, but had officially stepped onto the stage of history, possessing the qualifications to compete and vie for power.

"I’ve heard that Brother Anmin is proficient in medicine. Is that true?" After making small talk to establish a connection, Fu Wan, seeing that the atmosphere was just right, finally asked the question he most wanted to ask.

"I know a little, but I wouldn’t dare say I’m an expert. Does Lord Fu have a hidden ailment that needs treatment?" Lu Ming stroked his chin. "I don’t usually treat people easily, unless someone can persuade me. My lord, we’ve arrived at Wu Kuang’s residence."
Fu Wan wanted to say something more, but Lu Ming changed the subject. He thought, "Is this fellow trying to extort money?"
Treating patients is a normal thing, but a highly skilled physician wouldn’t treat people easily.
He had at least heard of a physician in Jingnan named Zhang Zhongjing, who was also a county magistrate. He rarely treated people, but his medical skills were exceptional.
Now that he needed a favor, he could only try to please him.

"Alright, Brother Anmin, please wait a moment. After I finish my business here, please come to my residence for a gathering. We hit it off immediately and are eager to have a long talk." Fu Wan extended the invitation, then led his soldiers to search the house.
The Wu residence erupted into chaos, filled with cries of distress and pleas for mercy.
To please Lu Ming, Fu Wan had ordered the soldiers conducting the search to thoroughly inventory Wu Kuang’s entire estate.
Money, antiques, decorations, vases—all were left untouched, as they were intended for Lu Ming.
Lu Ming, on the contrary, was delighted. Wu Kuang’s residence was in a prime location, and its gate was a massive five zhang wide, exuding grandeur.
Furthermore, the interior revealed a vast courtyard, many times larger than Wang Lang’s mansion.
The better the environment, the better one’s mood while living there.
Obtaining such a residence was quite a good thing.
And Emperor Ling and his allies certainly profited handsomely, obtaining a considerable sum from their ministers alone.
Unfortunately, this kind of scheme couldn’t be repeated, as everyone knew Lu Ming’s formidable fighting prowess and martial arts skills, and thus wouldn’t fall for it again.
They thought confiscating Wu Kuang’s property would be a difficult task, but before long, Fu Wan arrived with a steward. The steward had a rough idea of how many properties Wu Kuang owned.

chapters.title: Chapter 123 It’s so satisfying
paragraphs: "Brother Anmin, it’s confirmed. Besides this residence, Wu Kuang owns twelve shops on South Street and a workshop outside the city. You can check them out; they’re all yours now." Fu Wan handed a list to Lu Ming and called over the steward. "From now on, this is your master. This is Commandant Lu, understand?"
"Yes, sir." The middle-aged steward bowed deeply to Lu Ming with a mixture of fear and obsequious flattery. "I am Wu Ben, the former steward. Please give me any orders, sir."
Lu Ming glanced at the list casually and handed it to Fa Zheng behind him. "Xiaozhi, you handle this matter. Not a single penny can be lost. Go check on the shops too. I’ll handle things here. Go."
"Yes, sir." Fa Zheng found it rather strange and didn’t treat Lu Ming as his stepfather; that would be too awkward.

Putting aside the unpleasant first impression, Lu Ming was indeed a capable ruler with the potential of a wise monarch. His rise to power, step by step, was simply unbelievable to those from humble backgrounds.
However, there was one thing Fa Zheng felt he needed to discuss later: offending the Grand General and the Yuan family might make his future path difficult.
Professional matters should be left to professionals. Lu Ming needed a workshop to produce materials, which he could then sell for money.
This would allow him to support the wandering knights, whether to supplement his private army or to handle official business—a very good option.

"Lord Fu, I will certainly visit your residence another day, but I still need to visit the old Minister of Works today. Let’s talk another day," Lu Ming said, bringing up the Yang family, leaving the other party speechless.
"Very well, since there was a prior agreement, I won’t disturb you any longer." Fu Wan left decisively; having established a relationship, he would depart.

The reason for cultivating a relationship with Lu Ming was his exceptional medical skills, which could even, to some extent, reverse his disadvantage. Even the Yuan family sometimes had to bow down and make exchanges of benefits with Lu Ming.
Despite their differences, the exchange of benefits had to continue.
Everyone was busy. Emperor Ling was busy calculating how much money he had made.
The other ministers were busy discussing countermeasures, wondering whether to continue following the Yuan family’s lead or soften their stance and make contact with Lu Ming.
Being able to fight and heal was something many people desperately needed.

Everyone has some dental problems, but even a hundred doctors couldn’t find one that could cure toothache and tuberculosis. This revolutionary treatment method was destined to make him incredibly wealthy!
Lu Ming entered the residence and immediately saw the steward leading all the servants. The servants stood on the right, women in one line, men in another.

On the left were two elegant and beautiful women, and a woman with rosy lips, white teeth, a snow-white oval face, and large, watery almond-shaped eyes beneath willow-leaf eyebrows. Her timid expression made her seem like a frightened fawn, evoking pity.
"Who is this?"
Upon seeing Lu Ming, the beautiful woman’s eyes widened in surprise, then she quickly lowered her head. Faced with her husband’s murderer, she was powerless to do anything.
"Reporting to sir, this woman is the wife of the scoundrel Wu Kuang, Wu Yangshi," the steward Wu Ben introduced.
Upon hearing that she was Wu Kuang’s wife, Lu Ming’s eyes lit up. Good heavens! He hadn’t felt anything at first, but now that he was the wife of his enemy, he wasn’t about to miss out!
"And who is this?" Lu Ming asked, looking at the equally elegant woman beside him.
"Reporting to your Excellency, this is Zhang, the wife of Wu Kuang’s elder brother. Wu Kuang died young, and his wife took her family to live with him. This girl is Zhang’s daughter, Wu Xian."
Wu Xian!
Lu Ming was initially puzzled, but then, looking again, he suddenly remembered.
He loved the Three Kingdoms period and knew the characters in great detail.
This Wu Xian was Liu Bei’s wife after he entered Shu, and also the Queen of Shu!
He hadn’t expected to encounter her here; it was quite surprising.
At that moment, a messenger arrived, and a guard took the letter and handed it to Lu Ming.

Lu Ming glanced at it, quickly skimming its contents. He then coldly told his personal guards, "Tell the messenger that if Liu Yan wants to negotiate, he should come to me personally. Who does he think he is!"

His tone was extremely arrogant. Liu Yan was, after all, a member of the Han imperial family, and by seniority, an uncle of Emperor Ling. As a member of the Han imperial family, he held the position of Gentleman of the Palace and had served as Magistrate of Luoyang, Governor of Ji Province, Prefect of Nanyang, Minister of the Imperial Clan, and Grand Master of Ceremonies, among other official positions.
He was definitely not a Han imperial relative who was just coasting along; he was a capable man.
But even so, so what?
Lu Ming simply ignored him. As long as he clung to Emperor Ling’s coattails and generated benefits for the emperor, that was enough to maintain the status quo.
Plus, the Grand Commandant’s wife was promoting him and spreading her reputation for medical skills. Who doesn’t have someone suffering from illness?
They would all have to come to him for help. The world is driven by self-interest; in this way, who wanted to target him?
He only needed to repay favors with his medical skills to keep Liu Yan preoccupied with his own problems.
This was Lu Ming’s confidence; his reputation was established, and now it was time to build it up.
The waters of Luoyang were deep.
He decided to drain the water completely and see who was swimming naked!

"Everyone stay put. Continue what you were doing. If I find any dishonesty, I’ll send you all to the authorities and exile you to the frontier! Do you hear me!" Lu Ming didn’t mind keeping these people around; he needed manpower anyway. Instead, he instructed the steward to keep an eye out for anyone acting suspiciously and eliminate them when the opportunity arose.
There were definitely loyal servants among them; how far things would unfold remained to be seen.
Then, he hurriedly shoved Wu Kuang’s wife and his sister-in-law and daughter into the room. They were all experienced women; they could see through his intentions at a glance.
Yang Lian, however, never expected that at her age, with a son older than Lu Ming, he would still be interested in her!
For a moment, she didn’t know whether to be happy or sad!
Her husband and son were both murdered, and now she was forced to suffer humiliation beneath her enemy!
The thought was like a nightmare!

"Let me go! You insolent scoundrel! Do you know who I am?" Yang Lian was immediately forced onto the bed by Lu Ming. She struggled slightly, but was no match for him, and could only resort to intimidation using her status.
Being pinned down by a boy younger than her son was utterly shameful!

chapters.title: Chapter 128 Yang requested
paragraphs: Wu Yi had always served Liu Yan and was considered a promising young man.
Upon learning of his uncle’s defeat and death, he realized the gravity of the situation and sought Liu Yan’s help.
Liu Yan, showing him great respect, readily agreed to assist.
Now it seemed Lu Ming was in trouble.
Liu Yan was furious. He was the Grand Master of Ceremonies, a position of real power!

He held the highest position among the Nine Ministers, a very prestigious post, overseeing culture and education, the administration of imperial mausoleums, and also commanding the Imperial Academy and the Imperial Scholars.

He was primarily in charge of the rituals concerning heaven, earth, gods, and spirits, as well as auspicious and inauspicious rites, military and celebratory ceremonies, and the administration of artifacts such as jade, silk, bells, and drums.
He was about to take up his post in Yizhou, and yet he was being treated with such disrespect.

However, he had no choice but to help. Liu Yan harbored ambitions to become emperor himself, and a physiognomist predicted that Wu Yi’s sister, Lady Wu, would one day hold an extremely prestigious position. Therefore, he arranged for his son, Liu Mao, to marry Lady Wu.
Now a problem has arisen. Wu Xian has been included in the confiscation of her property and is now under Lu Ming’s command.
This wouldn’t normally be a problem; they could simply remove her.
However, Lu Ming isn’t giving them any face, so they’ll have to think of another way.

"Ziyuan, don’t worry, I’ll go and plead for her myself." Liu Yan truly harbors ambitions to become emperor, which is why he’s going to such lengths; otherwise, there would be no need to go through so much trouble for an outsider.
It’s a pity that Wu Xian, this future beauty with a noble status, has already been taken by Lu Ming!
She was deflowered, and he ejaculated inside her!
She might even be pregnant!
Even Liu Yan finds this hard to accept, but he doesn’t know yet, so he can only bite the bullet and go.
"Then I’ll trouble you, sir." Wu Yi also didn’t have a good solution. Although he hated Lu Ming, he didn’t have a better way to deal with it for the time being.
This is His Majesty’s decree. His Majesty is His Majesty, even if he is incompetent, he is still His Majesty.
When Liu Yan personally went to pay his respects, the steward only said, "Let’s talk about it tomorrow; Lu Ming has gone to a banquet at the Yang family’s residence."

This left Liu Yan speechless. The imperial clan was no match for the Yang family. The Yang family had been entrenched for many years and their influence was deeply entrenched; he couldn’t possibly contend with them.
The Yang family’s residence.
As soon as Lu Ming arrived, Yang Biao personally went to the gate to greet him, showing great courtesy.
Ordinary people wouldn’t be qualified to receive such treatment from him—not that it was unnecessary, but that he wasn’t qualified.
For him to do this, Lu Ming must have already demonstrated enough power to make them want to win him over.

"Grand Master, you are too kind. I have long admired you. It is truly an honor to meet you today!" Lu Ming immediately showered him with flattery, regardless of anything else, he just wanted to fawn over you first.
Yang Biao’s expression was rather indifferent. With the Yang family’s prestige and reputation, many people would fawn over him.
However, he only acted with courtesy because he needed Lu Ming’s help. "Anmin, you’re too kind. Please come in. We’ve prepared some simple wine; today’s victory deserves a hearty toast!"
"I’d be honored, please!"
"Please!"
After exchanging pleasantries, the two entered the main hall.
The decorations were luxurious, with silks and satins, and incomprehensible landscape paintings and calligraphy hanging on the walls.
The paper, seemingly made using some method, was inferior to plain white paper and crudely made, but still legible.

Musicians played, and dancers entered, bowing to the two men before beginning their dance to the music. Long sleeves flowing, red sleeves adding fragrance. Paired with fine wine and food, it was truly a delightful experience.

Lu Ming simply picked up his wine cup, offered a toast, and then began to eat. "Since you’ve sent me, sir, you must have something to instruct me on. Please speak freely. I will certainly not refuse if it is within my power!"
Simple, direct, and without any beating around the bush. Yang Biao’s impression of him deepened. "Anmin’s medical skills are superb. Could you examine my father?"

"I can, but I’ll need to see the situation. If there are no hidden illnesses, and he has simply passed away due to old age, then I have no way to help him." Lu Ming wouldn’t waste his time trying to prolong the man’s life; he could do so, but it wasn’t necessary.
"In any case, I will be very grateful." Yang Biao was somewhat dissatisfied. Was this an attempt to refuse?
"In that case, let’s begin." Lu Ming finished his wine in one gulp and stood up.
He had long known that Yang’s visit to him was never for anything good, and now it seemed it was indeed about treating an illness.
This was exactly what he expected: treat the sick, save lives, and then receive payment.
"Please." Yang Biao rose and personally led Lu Ming to the backyard.

They entered a room filled with the scent of sandalwood. A single stick of this sandalwood cost several taels of silver, an extremely high expense, and it only burned for an hour. Several sticks were needed a day, and at least five were required for each treatment to be effective.
Just from this, one could see the Yang family’s immense wealth. Perhaps not as rich as a country, but certainly not lacking in money!
Lu Ming approached the bedside and saw a gaunt old man, his eyes still closed.
He found it somewhat amusing, because Wang Lang was Yang Ci’s protégé, someone he was grooming.
He was also a collaborator with the Langya Wang family, and now that Wang Lang was imprisoned, and his wife and daughter had been seized and raped by Lu Ming, he was, in a sense, an enemy.
Lu Ming took Wang Lang’s pulse, narrowed his eyes, and inquired about some symptoms.

He then shook his head, and under Yang Biao’s expectant gaze, uttered the most desperate words, "This is tuberculosis, one of the incurable diseases. Unless Bian Que (a legendary physician) is resurrected, it’s unlikely to be cured!"
"What!" Yang Biao was shocked. The doctors in his family were always secretive and dared not speak openly. He had long suspected it, but he never expected it to be incurable!

"Although I cannot cure it, it shouldn’t be a problem to wait three to five years. In three to five years, perhaps there will be medicine that can cure it." Lu Ming didn’t make any absolute promises, because Yang Ci was already old, and medical conditions in ancient times were limited; a cure was extremely difficult. Therefore, he didn’t give any guarantees.
"Regardless, please do your utmost to treat him," Yang Biao said, clasping his hands in a fist salute. "I will certainly offer my gratitude."

"Then let’s observe again. I need to give the old man acupuncture to force out the remaining toxins. With rest and recuperation, he should live for another three to five years without any problem," Lu Ming said, pulling out silver needles and beginning to heat them. This method struck Yang Biao as very strange, but he didn’t ask. Perhaps it was Lu Ming’s secret technique; everyone has their hidden tricks up their sleeve!
It took about an hour, and by the time it was finished, it was already evening.

"What!" Liu Yan was dumbfounded. This was too fast! His noble daughter-in-law was gone? She’d been used? How could he possibly let his son marry someone who’d been with another woman?
During the Eastern Han Dynasty, women were encouraged to remarry, all for the sake of population growth.
Moreover, not remarrying was punishable. While the punishment had been relaxed somewhat by this time, it still existed.
Marriage was certainly possible, but Liu Yan himself was somewhat displeased. What kind of status did he have? How could his son marry a "second-hand" woman?
"I beg you, Commandant, to be lenient. It’s not too late. Let them leave." Liu Yan still maintained his airs, offering no favors, and expecting them to be released with just a word?

"My lord, this is my concubine. What right do you have to release her? Living in Wu Kuang’s house makes her Wu Kuang’s family. His Majesty issued an imperial decree bestowing Wu Kuang’s family property upon me. You, my lord, can order her release with a single word? Does your word carry more weight than His Majesty’s? In that case, my lord, please come with me to the palace to see the Emperor and let him judge this matter. Come, my lord, let’s go!" Lu Ming finished speaking and grabbed Liu Yan’s sleeve, indicating they were going to the palace to see the Emperor.
Liu Yan never expected Lu Ming to act like such a troublemaker, exploding at the slightest provocation. Couldn’t he speak properly?
If it were any other matter, even if it reached Emperor Ling, at most he would receive a mild reprimand.
They were all from the same clan; the Liu family’s empire needed them.
But now, when Emperor Ling was in a good mood, to ask him to retract his words and contradict himself was simply ridiculous!
Liu Yan didn’t have that kind of face or influence!
"Hmph, since Commandant Lu refuses, then so be it. Farewell." Liu Yan certainly wouldn’t risk offending him; that would be courting death, not seeking personal gain.
"Commander Lu is truly young and impetuous, full of youthful arrogance!"
This wasn’t a compliment; it was sarcasm. Youthful arrogance rarely ends well. Young people should learn from their mistakes; otherwise, they, the older generation, would seem foolish!
"Heh, is a young man without arrogance?" Lu Ming sneered. "Goodbye!"
After leaving the residence, Liu Yan gritted his teeth. "How dare this brat! Just you wait!"
Just as Liu Yan left, an unexpected person appeared.
Lu Ming saw Cao Cao, led in by a servant. Short in stature, with a sallow complexion, Cao Aman, though possessing an air of arrogance, had yet to display his talents.
"So it’s Mengde visiting! What an honor! Please have a seat!" Lu Ming said with a cupped hand.
"I’ve come uninvited, please don’t take offense, Brother Anmin," Cao Cao said with a smile. Although not physically imposing, he possessed a rare personal charm.

"What brings you here, Brother Mengde?" Lu Ming asked directly after sitting down. Seemingly to ease the atmosphere, he added, "His Majesty has ordered me to examine Princess Wannian. It’s urgent, not a matter of urging you to leave."

"Oh! I see. Brother Anmin, you are truly multi-talented! I have no urgent business to attend to, but I’ve heard you’re going to Hedong to recruit soldiers. I’d like to accompany you. What do you say?" Cao Cao wasn’t there to recruit soldiers, but simply to cultivate a good relationship with Lu Ming.
His keen eye told him Lu Ming was no ordinary man; befriending him would certainly not be a loss.
"Very well, I’ll visit Mengde’s residence another day for a chat. That’s enough for today, I still need to examine the princess." Lu Ming readily agreed; he had no intention of recruiting Cao Cao.
Such a person, even just talking to Cao Cao for a while would be pleasant.
He possesses an extremely charismatic personality and would never submit to anyone.
However, those who defile other men’s wives and daughters will also have their wives and daughters defiled; every cause has its effect, and Cao Cao’s retribution is mine!
Although abrupt, Cao Cao had no choice but to comply.
He was merely passing by and came to visit on a whim.
This was actually quite impolite. A formal visit requires sending a formal invitation and scheduling an appointment; that is proper etiquette.
Such a sudden visit, unless it’s an acquaintance, is truly impolite.
He arranged for Jiang Xin to recruit wandering knights, while Fa Zheng was responsible for supervising the workshop’s progress.
And those shopfronts also needed to be utilized; only by utilizing them well could they be profitable.
Lu Ming’s choice was to engage in some trading. Merchanting was considered a lowly profession, but without it, he would starve.
Selling lamb skewers would be a good option. Next, Lu Ming needed to gather ingredients to make a hot pot.
In this era, pork was the primary meat, while lamb was the main cut in the north. Only the royal family could afford beef.
Oxen were not allowed to be slaughtered; only the royal family could eat them.
And regardless of whether it was a domestic pig or a goat, the offal was never eaten.
Firstly, there was no way to process it, and secondly, it was too gamey and unpalatable. Only the extremely poor would consume it.
Raw materials were being continuously transported to the mansion, and there was enough money to cover expenses.
At least for two months, Lu Ming wouldn’t need to worry about finances.
The servants in the mansion needed monthly wages, and the mansion’s expenses, the women’s necessities, and groceries all required funds.
There was a small vegetable garden in the main garden, but it was abandoned; after all, vegetables grown there don’t taste very good.
Everything was proceeding smoothly, so Lu Ming took the imperial edict and headed to Princess Wannian’s residence.
Historically, records about this princess are extremely scarce. All that is known is that she was Emperor Ling’s daughter, and his only daughter.
Her husband is not recorded, nor is the Holy Mother.
Everything seems like a mystery, or perhaps she didn’t wield much influence at all, merely possessing a royal title that allowed her to be mentioned briefly in historical records, but that was all.

chapters.title: Chapter 132 Visiting Princess Wannian
paragraphs: Arriving at the princess’s residence wasn’t far; it was only a twenty-minute walk from Lu Ming’s newly acquired mansion. This was on horseback; on foot, it would have taken almost an hour.
The princess’s residence was somewhat deserted. After a servant announced his arrival, the steward, a robust woman, quickly came and invited Lu Ming into the mansion.
The princess’s residence was quite large, no smaller than his own. As the only daughter of the Emperor, her living conditions were quite good.
Lu Ming walked through the courtyard before reaching the main hall. After being told to wait, he sat down and closed his eyes.
He hated waiting; it was a waste of time for him. He’d rather use that time for something beneficial.
After waiting for a while, footsteps approached. The steward woman then said, "Her Highness the Princess wishes to ask you a few questions. If you can answer them, you will be granted an audience."
"Please speak," Lu Ming opened his eyes. Interesting. They were using this tactic against him? "How foolish!"
"May I ask, Doctor, how should a cold be treated?" the housekeeper asked, holding a piece of paper in her hand, presumably containing the answer.

"Everyone is different; there’s no single treatment. The main symptoms are coughing, a sore throat, thin, white phlegm, no thirst, headache, no sweating, pale red tongue with a white coating, and a floating or tight pulse."

"Colds are further divided into overexertion and typhoid fever. Overexertion requires rest and recuperation, along with medicinal diets. Typhoid fever requires keeping warm and protected from wind, along with medicinal diets."
Before the housekeeper could answer, a clear female voice followed, "May I ask, Doctor, what is the prescription?"
"This is a closely guarded secret, difficult to disclose." Lu Ming wasn’t foolish enough to reveal the prescription directly.
Colds were very difficult to cure in ancient times, even during the Three Kingdoms period, and only in modern times did the situation improve slightly.
With the sound of footsteps, a beautiful woman dressed in white silk and satin slowly entered.
Behind her were two other elegant women, one of whom possessed the air of a noble lady. Her face was charming, and although she remained silent, her entire demeanor exuded an alluring aura.
"This Princess Wannian greets you, sir," the woman in silk and satin bowed slightly to Lu Ming, the respect evident in her medical expertise.

"This humble official is Lu Ming, a military officer, greetings to Your Highness. May I ask what ailment Your Highness requires my attention? Please speak freely. The more detailed your description, the better the treatment. Otherwise, without a clear understanding of the illness, even if Bian Que were resurrected, he would find it difficult to cure," Lu Ming said respectfully, bowing his head. He was still somewhat amazed by Princess Wannian!
However, he was even more astonished by the attendant behind Princess Wannian, wondering who this extraordinary woman was!
"The cold you mentioned earlier is it," Princess Wannian said, taking her seat in the superior position, still kneeling.
The loose silk robe, worn by her bent-over kneeling posture, accentuated the alluring curve of her buttocks, making Lu Ming’s eyes water!
He truly had little resistance to women. As a lecherous devil, his motto was "No woman is too good to be true," wishing he could have his way with every woman in the world and impregnate them all!

"May I ask if it’s from overexertion or an infection caused by chills? When did Your Highness contract the illness, and what are your current symptoms? Please extend your hand; I need to take your pulse and examine you." Lu Ming took out a pillow from his medicine box, asking questions as he did so.
"I don’t know, the doctor will know after examining me," Princess Wannian’s voice was clear and melodious, like a lark. She herself possessed an ethereal quality, almost otherworldly.
Lu Ming placed his hand on Princess Wannian’s wrist, closed his eyes, and began to take her pulse. He already knew, using his diagnostic skills, that the infection was caused by a chill.

"Your Highness, I need to understand the situation clearly before I begin a consultation. Even when treating His Majesty, this is the case. Therefore, please forgive any abruptness. If the princess cannot accept this, she may resign."
This was a clear statement of intent; if she could accept it, she would treat him. If not, she could dismiss him immediately and leave the matter alone.
Princess Wannian didn’t realize this was a trap; she thought it was just a standard answer.
Later, she realized how cunning he was.
Having already brought up the Emperor Ling, even the princess had nothing to say.
"Doctor, please ask away."
After a long wait, Lu Ming stopped taking her pulse, still with his eyes closed, deep in thought.
Princess Wannian, growing increasingly impatient, finally spoke, "Your aura is weak; you need nourishment. Has Your Highness been engaging in sexual activity frequently lately?"
Upon hearing this question, the two beautiful attendants were taken aback, their faces flushing red.
Princess Wannian, however, was somewhat embarrassed and angry. "Doctor, are you perhaps teasing me? Disrespecting the royal family—you cannot bear such a crime!"
Lu Ming, on the other hand, looked at Princess Wannian with a strange expression, his face calm and without the slightest panic.

"Your Highness, why do you say such a thing? I asked the same question when I treated His Majesty. Mencius said, ’Food and sex are human nature; they are inherent and should not be restrained.’ Do you think this is flirting? You are sorely mistaken. Excessive sexual activity depletes the body, making it more susceptible to illness from wind and cold. Insufficient sexual activity leads to stagnation and may even corrode the body. From a medical perspective, let’s be frank. If Your Highness cannot accept this, I reiterate my point: please resign. I have treated countless patients, including kings and generals."
Faced with Lu Ming’s earnest nonsense, Princess Wannian was speechless.
If an ordinary physician had said such a thing, he would have been thrown out and handed over to the authorities for allegedly disrespecting a princess.
However, Lu Ming was the physician who treated Emperor Ling, possessing such authority, thus his words carried a degree of credibility.
Princess Wannian felt somewhat ashamed and indignant. She glared at Lu Ming, then said to her two female attendants, "Wenji, Yulan, you two should go back now. We’ll discuss medicine another day."
"Yes, Your Highness." The two women bowed to Princess Wannian. Although they wanted to stay, the princess had already told them to leave; how could they say anything more and invite trouble?
If they angered the princess, it wouldn’t be fun.
Hearing the two names, Lu Ming glanced a few more times at the beautiful and elegant young lady. Could it be Cai Wenji?

chapters.title: Chapter 133 The three women’s discussion
paragraphs: The other one was unknown. Lu Ming’s eyes flickered as he looked on, his thoughts unreadable.
Princess Wannian seemed to notice Lu Ming’s gaze, or perhaps she was removing him from their list of potential conquests.

"Her name is Cai Wenji, the daughter of Cai Yong, the General of the Palace Attendants, betrothed to the Wei family of Hedong. The other is Zhang Yulan, daughter of Zhang Heng, who abstained from alcohol; her ancestors were descendants of Marquis Liu."
Marquis Liu was Zhang Liang. The descendants of Zhang Liang had enjoyed a glorious past, and although their fortunes had declined, they were still doing reasonably well.
As for Cai Wenji, there’s not much to say. A truly pitiful talented woman, she was first married to a consumptive husband who died soon after.

Later, during the rebellions in Guanzhong caused by Dong Zhuo and Li Jue, the Southern Xiongnu, a vassal state, seized the opportunity to rebel and plunder, and Cai Yan was captured by the Xiongnu’s Left Wise King.
Cai Yan lived in the north for twelve years before being redeemed by Cao Cao and remarrying.
Unfortunately, her happiness was short-lived; her husband committed another crime, and she had no choice but to plead with Cao Cao for help, but nothing came of it.
Such a beautiful woman, yet her life was so tragic.
Lu Ming felt an urge to take Cai Wenji into his arms and make her his concubine.
Beautiful and learned, he would truly regret missing out!

"So it’s them. Before coming, I heard that Her Highness was surrounded by talented women. Birds of a feather flock together, and Her Highness is also a talented woman." Lu Ming nodded, feigning understanding.
In truth, he knew nothing about them and felt nothing at all.
He simply thought those two women were quite attractive.
Young widows, even better.
Since they were widows, he had to work even harder to get them!
"Alright, Doctor, you can ask your questions now." Princess Wannian didn’t want to ramble on. If Emperor Ling hadn’t summoned Lu Ming, she probably wouldn’t have even seen him.
"Do you cough often?" Lu Ming’s questions became quite normal again.
"No." Princess Wannian lowered her head, not looking at Lu Ming—perhaps she didn’t want to, or perhaps she disdained to look.
"Do you feel cold?" Lu Ming took out his silver needles and fiddled with them, seemingly casually.
"Occasionally at night."
"Do you shiver when you feel cold?"
"No."
The two exchanged questions, occasionally venturing into more challenging situations. Princess Wannian answered calmly, trying her best not to get angry.
"So, I understand. One last question: Does the Princess have frequent sexual activity?" Lu Ming nodded, took out a piece of paper, and wrote the names of medicinal herbs on it.
Upon hearing this question, Princess Wannian frowned again, looking at Lu Ming with displeasure. "Do you think I’m a promiscuous woman?"
"Why do you say that, Princess?" Lu Ming felt a little strange and retorted with a serious attitude.
"My husband has been dead for many years. I don’t have any lovers. Haven’t you heard that?" Princess Wannian was seething with anger. Did he think she was a promiscuous and impure woman?
Outrageous!
She was, after all, a princess, not a fickle woman. She wouldn’t do such things.
Seeing this, Lu Ming’s expression became somewhat strange.

"Since arriving in Luoyang, I’ve been busy with official duties and have never had time for personal matters, much less for gossiping. I truly didn’t know Your Highness was a widow. This was my oversight."
Hearing Lu Ming’s explanation, Princess Wannian was still somewhat dissatisfied. No one would be happy to be considered a promiscuous woman. "Doctor, please be careful with your words and actions."

"A doctor’s heart is selfless; everything is for the sake of healing. If it weren’t for treatment, I wouldn’t be asking these questions. One last question: how often does the princess masturbate?" Lu Ming had barely finished speaking when he saw Princess Wannian’s gentle expression turn ferocious; this gentle princess seemed about to explode.

So he hurriedly explained, "Mencius said, ’Food and sex are human nature,’ and ancient records state that sexual intercourse can bring physical and mental comfort, improve circulation, and detoxify and beautify the skin. This is not flirting. His Majesty engages in sexual intercourse daily; this is the natural order. Princess, please do not worry."
Princess Wannian was furious. A man asking a woman such a question was clearly flirting. "You lecherous scoundrel! Get out!"
Lu Ming immediately bowed and said, "Please trouble Your Highness to write a letter of resignation. I can also reply to His Majesty when I treat him."
Princess Wannian was about to explode on the spot, but then, as if remembering something, she said, "Enough! Go away. I don’t want to see you again."
